story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的面包心事

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In the park, the user stands at the big route map, tracing a path toward the bridge in the distance.
beats.chinese: 公园里，用户站在大路线图前，手指描向远处的桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a cycling jacket stops nearby, holding a small sealed bag of plain bread. He glances at the food icons printed along the map's edge.
beats.chinese: 一个穿骑行外套的男人在旁边停下，手里提着一小袋密封的普通面包。他瞥见地图边上印的餐饮图标。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you're reading that the right way round. Most folk turn it twice first. The bridge route's the good one, for what it's worth.
beats.chinese: 啊，你地图拿的方向是对的。大多数人得转两圈。说真的，走桥那条路最好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — not interrupting, am I? I only came over because of those little fork symbols. They've put me in a mood, so they have.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——没打扰你吧？我走过来就是因为那些小叉子图标。它们让我有点心痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the bread bag slightly, as if presenting evidence.
beats.chinese: 他微微举起面包袋，像在出示证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is plain white bread. I spent about two years telling people I hated it. Bought a bag this week anyway. This week or generally — those are different answers.
beats.chinese: 这是普通白面包。我花了大概两年跟人说我不喜欢它。这周还是买了。这周和一般来说——是两个不同的答案。

choices.english: Ask him: was it actually bad before, or something else?
choices.chinese: 问他：以前不吃是因为不好吃，还是别的原因？

choices.english: Ask if he'll just buy it again until he gets sick of it once more.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会一直买到又吃腻为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bad? No, no. It was grand, the whole time. That's the annoying part.
beats.chinese: 不好吃？不，不。一直都挺好的。烦就烦在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts the bag to his other hand and leans against the map frame.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子换到另一只手，靠在地图框上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just didn't want it. For months. Nothing happened, no bad sandwich, nothing. The want switched off like a lamp.
beats.chinese: 我就是不想吃了。好几个月。什么都没发生，没有难吃的三明治，没有。那个念头像灯一样关了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But my mates filed it under 'Declan hates bread.' Permanent blacklist. So now when it's back on the menu, they look at me like I've grown a second head.
beats.chinese: 但我朋友们把它记成了'Declan讨厌面包'。永久黑名单。所以现在它又回到菜单上，他们看我的眼神像多了个脑袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, the shrug almost audible.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，那耸肩几乎能听见声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I never corrected them, did I. Easier to push the sandwich round the plate than say 'not today.' Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 我也从没纠正过他们，对吧。在盘子里推着三明治，比说一句'今天不了'容易。啊，你懂的。

choices.english: Suggest next time he just say he doesn't feel like it lately.
choices.chinese: 建议他下次直接说只是最近不想吃。

choices.english: Ask whether getting back into it feels like proving himself wrong.
choices.chinese: 问重新喜欢上的时候，会不会觉得自己打脸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, almost certainly. That's the pattern. Six weeks of this bag, then I won't look at a bakery for a season.
beats.chinese: 哦，几乎肯定。就是这个规律。这袋面包吃六周，然后我一整个季节不进面包店。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the bag a small, fond shake.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻晃了晃袋子，带点喜爱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to fight it. Made rules, rotation charts, the lot. Now I just enjoy it while it's here.
beats.chinese: 我以前跟它较劲。定规矩、排轮换表，全套。现在它还在的时候我就好好享受。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No forced schedule either. The craving leaves when it leaves. I'd rate this bread nine out of ten and still never order it again, come the day.
beats.chinese: 也不给自己定强制周期。念头走了就是走了。这面包我能打九分，到了那天照样再也不点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the bridge route on the map, then back at the bag.
beats.chinese: 他看看地图上的桥路线，又看看袋子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trick is not treating it like a promise. It's just lunch. Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就是别把它当成承诺。这只是顿饭。啊，你懂的。

choices.english: Say he should enjoy this bag now, while he likes it.
choices.chinese: 说现在喜欢就先好好享受这一袋。

choices.english: Ask if he minds friends still eating things he's gone off.
choices.chinese: 问他介不介意朋友继续吃他已经吃腻的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands up straight, trying the sentence out like a new word.
beats.chinese: 他站直了，试着把那句话像生词一样念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Not today — ask me again in a month.' Hm. Say it like that, no big speech after it.
beats.chinese: '今天不了——一个月后再问我。'嗯。就这么说，后面不用长篇解释。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's lighter than listing reasons, isn't it? Reasons just start an argument. This just ends one.
beats.chinese: 这比列一堆理由轻松，对吧？理由只会引来争论。这句话直接结束争论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the bread bag under his arm, keeping it with him.
beats.chinese: 他把面包袋夹在胳膊下，还是自己带着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Bridge route, bread in the bag, and a new sentence for the lads. Good map, this. Thanks for standing still long enough.
beats.chinese: 好。走桥那条路，面包在袋里，还有一句给兄弟们的新话。这地图不错。谢谢你站这儿听我说完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs before answering, the kind that admits the hit landed.
beats.chinese: 他先笑了才回答，那种承认被说中的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They'll absolutely take the mickey. Two years of 'no bread for Declan,' and now I'm queueing for a roll. I'll never hear the end of it.
beats.chinese: 他们肯定会笑我。两年'面包与Declan无缘'，现在我在排队买面包。这事他们能笑到明年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the bag once, firm, like closing an argument.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍袋子，很干脆，像结束一场辩论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'm not giving up good bread to stay consistent with a story I never told properly. Let them laugh. It's still a good roll.
beats.chinese: 但我不会为了跟一个自己都没讲对的故事保持一致，就放弃好吃的面包。让他们笑。面包还是好吃的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, being laughed at over lunch is cheap. Suffering through a sandwich I don't want — that's the expensive one.
beats.chinese: 说真的，为一顿饭被人笑，代价很小。硬吃一个不想要的三明治——那才贵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at the bridge path and lifts the bag in a small farewell.
beats.chinese: 他朝桥的路点点头，举起袋子算是小小的道别。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this, then nods slowly, like agreeing with a sensible score.
beats.chinese: 他想想，然后缓缓点头，像同意一个合理的评分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. That's very fair. It's good bread. Why am I planning its funeral while it's still in my hand?
beats.chinese: 有道理。非常有道理。面包是好的。它还在我手里呢，我干嘛先安排它的葬礼？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grips the bag more firmly and squares his shoulders toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子握得更稳，朝桥的方向挺了挺肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the nice thing — nobody's asking me what I'll want next month. Not you, not the lads. Today I want bread. That's the whole job just now.
beats.chinese: 还有个好地方——没人问我下个月想吃什么。你没有，兄弟们也没有。今天我想吃面包。这就是眼下的全部任务。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, bridge it is. Enjoy your map. Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 好，就走桥了。祝你地图看得开心。啊，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off on foot at his usual brisk walk, bag swinging, without looking back for approval.
beats.chinese: 他迈着惯常的轻快步子出发，袋子晃着，没有回头寻求认同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves the question off like it's the easiest one all day.
beats.chinese: 他摆摆手，像这是今天最简单的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: God, no. Eat away. My appetite's my problem, not a club rule.
beats.chinese: 天哪，不介意。尽管吃。我的胃口是我自己的事，又不是俱乐部规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've sat with mates through whole meals I didn't want, just drinking water and taking the mick out of them. Happy days, honestly.
beats.chinese: 我跟朋友坐过整整顿饭，自己不想吃，就喝着水调侃他们。说实话，挺开心的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the map's food icons with the bread bag, almost like a small toast.
beats.chinese: 他用面包袋指了指地图上的餐饮图标，像小小的举杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same table, different plates — that's the whole secret, if there is one. Nobody has to match anybody.
beats.chinese: 同一张桌子，不同的盘子——如果有秘诀，这就是全部了。谁也不用跟谁一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before this bag talks me into a second one. Good luck with the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好，我得走了，趁这袋面包还没劝我再买一袋。祝桥路顺利。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 果汁厂感官测试员Declan，工作味觉可靠，私人胃口却周期分明。他在公园地图旁坦白自己重新爱上了白面包，朋友们却把他记成永久讨厌面包。四条分支里，他或学会一句干脆的'今天不了'，或坦然接受被笑，或先享受眼前这袋，或大方允许同桌不同口味。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user is back at the route map, tracing the bridge line again. Nearby, Declan folds a small empty bread bag — the same sealed one — flat and tucks it into his backpack.
beats.chinese: 用户回到路线图前，手指又描起那条桥路线。旁边，Declan把那只空了的密封面包袋折小，塞进背包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bag didn't make it past the bridge. Meant to last the whole walk. It lasted the bridge.
beats.chinese: 那袋面包没撑过桥。本来打算走完全程的。结果走到桥就没了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the backpack pocket, confirming it's empty, and shrugs.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍背包口袋，确认空了，耸耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you know yourself. The phase was still on. It's gone quicker than planned, but I'm not apologising to a bag of bread.
beats.chinese: 啊，你懂的。那个念头还在。吃得比计划快，但我不会向一袋面包道歉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the map once, points at the bridge, and heads off at his easy pace.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一眼地图，指指桥，迈着轻松的步子走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, no bread, no problem. Ask me again in a month.
beats.chinese: 好，没面包，没关系。一个月后再问我。

card.name: Declan Maher
card.occupation: Sensory testing assistant at a juice plant
card.personality: Declan is easygoing in a way that can look like agreement when it isn't. He's genuinely pleasant company, quick with a joke, but his appetites run in strong, unapologetic cycles: he'll eat the same lunch for six weeks straight, then hit a wall and not want to see it for months. He finds this funny about himself, mostly, though he hates the awkward moment when a friend proudly orders his old favourite and he has to pretend. He separates work from taste cleanly — at the plant he's scrupulously objective, at home he's hopeless and happy.
card.background: Declan grew up in Drogheda, the middle of three, in a house where dinner was the same rotation every fortnight and nobody thought anything of it. He moved to Dublin in his twenties, drifted through a few warehouse jobs, then landed at a juice plant as a sensory testing assistant, where his palate turned out to be genuinely reliable. Colleagues trust his scores; friends assume that means he knows what he wants to eat, which he doesn't. His private appetite swings wildly — a burrito phase, a long black-pudding summer, then nothing. He's learned to say 'not today' rather than explain, though he still occasionally suffers through a meal out of politeness.
card.speechStyle: Dry, quick, self-deprecating; short sentences with a shrug built in, often trailing into 'ah, you know yourself.'
card.signature: Ah, not today — ask me again in a month.

content.summaryZh: 果汁厂感官测试员Declan，工作味觉可靠，私人胃口却周期分明。他在公园地图旁坦白自己重新爱上了白面包，朋友们却把他记成永久讨厌面包。四条分支里，他或学会一句干脆的'今天不了'，或坦然接受被笑，或先享受眼前这袋，或大方允许同桌不同口味。

card.name: Declan Maher
card.occupation: Sensory testing assistant at a juice plant
card.personality: Declan is easygoing in a way that can look like agreement when it isn't. He's genuinely pleasant company, quick with a joke, but his appetites run in strong, unapologetic cycles: he'll eat the same lunch for six weeks straight, then hit a wall and not want to see it for months. He finds this funny about himself, mostly, though he hates the awkward moment when a friend proudly orders his old favourite and he has to pretend. He separates work from taste cleanly — at the plant he's scrupulously objective, at home he's hopeless and happy.
card.background: Declan grew up in Drogheda, the middle of three, in a house where dinner was the same rotation every fortnight and nobody thought anything of it. He moved to Dublin in his twenties, drifted through a few warehouse jobs, then landed at a juice plant as a sensory testing assistant, where his palate turned out to be genuinely reliable. Colleagues trust his scores; friends assume that means he knows what he wants to eat, which he doesn't. His private appetite swings wildly — a burrito phase, a long black-pudding summer, then nothing. He's learned to say 'not today' rather than explain, though he still occasionally suffers through a meal out of politeness.
card.speechStyle: Dry, quick, self-deprecating; short sentences with a shrug built in, often trailing into 'ah, you know yourself.'
card.signature: Ah, not today — ask me again in a month.

card.name: Dolores Camacho
card.occupation: city sculpture cleaning crew
hobbies: slow laps at the municipal pool
card.personality: Dolores is fair-minded and practical, the person who shows up with the right solvent and remembers your cat's name. Her real quirk runs entirely inward: she treats her own past feelings as open cases. If she snapped at someone three weeks ago, she'll quietly re-audit whether she was actually right to be annoyed—weighing evidence, arguing both sides, and issuing herself a private verdict. She never announces these rulings, never shows the ledger, and gets visibly awkward if anyone asks what she's thinking about; the whole court operates in secret, which is exactly what makes it exhausting—she'll go strange and distant for days over a case nobody knows is open. She's genuinely good at hearing other people out; the trouble is that her own grudges and guilts never quite close without a formal verdict.
card.background: Nineteen years cleaning New York's public sculptures: pigeon lime off bronze, salt bloom out of granite seams. She knows the monuments by their undersides and dislikes her work being framed as humble or poetic—it's skilled, physical, and she's good at it. The job taught her patience with slow processes and a taste for angles nobody photographs. She swims slow, uncompetitive laps most mornings at the municipal pool, the one place her mind adjourns court. Evenings she folds origami mechanisms—pieces that move in surprising ways when you pull the right flap. She lives in Queens with a cat named Pigeon. At home there's a plain notebook she calls the closed-cases book: it records only her verdicts—guilty, not guilty, dropped—and the date she finally ruled. She has never shown it to anyone and isn't sure she ever will.
card.speechStyle: Plain, warm, unhurried. She asks a real question before offering an opinion. Dry humor, concrete details, no speeches. Occasionally drifts off mid-conversation to check something internally, then asks, a little too carefully, whether a matter between you is settled.
card.signature: Hold on—are we square on that? I just want to be sure it's closed.

beats.chinese: 她安静地做了一会儿，每道折痕都用拇指平面压两遍。折错的地方压平了，形状重新归位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. Back on track. You keep writing—don't mind me. Who's the postcard for, if you don't mind me asking? Just curious what people still bother mailing.
beats.chinese: 好了，回到正轨。你继续写，别管我。方便问一句，明信片写给谁？就是好奇还有人愿意寄信。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts the paper so its moving flap faces the pond, away from your notebook, and keeps her elbows tucked in.
beats.chinese: 她把纸调了个方向，让会动的那片朝向池塘，避开你的本子，手肘也收了回去。

choices.english: Keep writing your own postcard.
choices.chinese: 继续写自己的卡片。

choices.english: Ask how the paper mechanism actually moves.
choices.chinese: 问纸机关是怎样动的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Old things? Sure. I re-watch my own reactions sometimes—like, did I actually have a point, or was I just tired that day. That kind of old thing.
beats.chinese: 旧事？当然。我有时会重看自己的反应——比如我当时到底有没有道理，还是那天只是累了。就是那种旧事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the corrected corner back into place and holds the half-finished piece up to the light, checking the layers line up.
beats.chinese: 她把修正好的角折回原位，把半成品举到光线下，检查各层是否对齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The specific one I was chewing on just now? I'd rather keep that to myself, no offense. It's already mostly dealt with.
beats.chinese: 刚才在琢磨的那件具体的事？我想自己留着，别见怪。它基本已经处理完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a paperwork habit, mostly. Boring stuff. Doesn't stop my hands, as you can see.
beats.chinese: 主要就是个案头习惯。挺无聊的。你看，也不耽误手上的活。

choices.english: Say there's no need to share any details.
choices.chinese: 表示不必说细节。

choices.english: Ask whether it ever affects the work she's doing with her hands.
choices.chinese: 问这样会不会影响手上做事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You go back to the postcard. Dolores works beside you, unhurried, the only sounds pen scratches and the soft press of creases.
beats.chinese: 你回到明信片上。多洛雷斯在旁边不紧不慢地折着，只有笔的沙沙声和压折痕的轻响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice, actually. Two people, two quiet jobs, nobody performing anything.
beats.chinese: 这样其实挺好。两个人，两件安静的活儿，谁也不用表演什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the side flap one last time. The paper opens wide, then closes with a clean snap, every layer sitting where it should.
beats.chinese: 她最后一次拉侧面的折片。纸大大地打开，又干脆地合上，每一层都待在它该在的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Closed properly. Thanks for the quiet—it did the trick.
beats.chinese: 好了。妥当地收工了。谢谢你的安静，真管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How it moves? Watch. This flap here is the trigger. I pull it, and this inside panel swings on a hidden fold—open, shut. All one sheet, no glue.
beats.chinese: 它怎么动的？看好了。这片是开关。我一拉，里面这块板就绕一道暗折痕转——开，合。就一张纸，不用胶水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She demonstrates once, slowly, tilting it so you can see the inner panel swing on its fold. Then she holds it still again.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢演示了一次，倾斜着让你看清里面那块板绕折痕转动。然后又把它放平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's just geometry doing the work. I like that a flat thing remembers a shape you pressed into it. No glue, no staples. It holds because of the creases.
beats.chinese: 其实就是几何在干活。我喜欢一张平纸能记住你压进去的形状。不用胶水，不用钉书钉。它靠折痕立住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Took me three evenings to learn this one. The trick is pressing every fold twice. Once isn't enough for the memory.
beats.chinese: 这个我学了三个晚上。诀窍是每道折痕压两遍。一遍不够，记不住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Dolores sets the paper down for a moment and rolls her shoulders. Something in her posture lets go.
beats.chinese: 多洛雷斯把纸放下片刻，转了转肩膀。她的姿势里有什么东西松开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Appreciate that. Most people push a little, you know. You didn't, and that lands well with me.
beats.chinese: 多谢你这样。你知道，多数人会追问一点。你没有，这让我很舒服。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the paper back up and finishes the last two folds without hurry, then slides it into her jacket pocket, flat and safe.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起纸，不慌不忙地折完最后两道，然后把它平平地放进外套口袋，放得妥妥帖帖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. I'll leave you to your postcard. Good luck with the stamp—those corner boxes bite.
beats.chinese: 好了。你继续写明信片吧。祝邮票顺利——那四个角的小格子可咬人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it affect my hands? Honestly, sometimes. That wrong fold a minute ago? That was exactly that. My hands were here, my head was three weeks back.
beats.chinese: 影响手上做事吗？说实话，有时候会。刚才那个折错的地方？就是这个原因。手在这儿，脑子在三周前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at the crease she corrected earlier, still slightly lighter than the others on the paper's surface.
beats.chinese: 她指了指刚才修正的那道折痕，在纸面上仍比别的折痕浅一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the fix is the same either way. Unfold it, flatten it, re-crease it straight. Paper forgives if you catch it early.
beats.chinese: 不过解决办法都一样。展开，压平，重新折正。纸这东西，发现得早就肯原谅你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She re-aligns the edges against each other, taps them square, and gives the side flap a test pull. It opens and shuts, clean.
beats.chinese: 她把纸边互相对齐，敲正，试拉了一下侧面的折片。开合干脆利落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Back in working order. Good question, though. Not many people ask what a thing costs the person doing it.
beats.chinese: 好了。恢复正常运转。不过这问题问得好。没几个人会问一件事让做的人付出了什么。

content.summaryZh: 纽约雕塑清洗工多洛雷斯在池塘边折会动的折纸机关，走神折错方向，低声承认在想一件已过去的小事。四条分支里她或安静收工、或演示机关开合、或因被尊重而松快、或坦承走神偶尔误手，边界清晰，温暖不煽情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone ledge by the pond. You sit there writing a postcard, pen moving across the card. A little way off, Dolores is looking at her phone in both hands, laughing quietly at the screen.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边那块石台。你坐在那儿写明信片，笔在卡片上移动。不远处，多洛雷斯双手捧着手机，对着屏幕低声笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hey. Come look at this idiot. This is Pigeon—cat, not bird, long story—and this morning there was an actual pigeon on my windowsill.
beats.chinese: 哦，嘿。来看看这个笨蛋。这是鸽子——是猫，不是鸟，说来话长——今天早上我窗台上落了只真鸽子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The real pigeon's out there doing its whole pigeon show, and Pigeon just turned her back on the window and went to sleep in the laundry basket. Zero professional curiosity.
beats.chinese: 真鸽子在外面表演全套鸽子节目，鸽子（猫）却背对窗户，钻进洗衣篮睡觉了。一点职业好奇心都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scrolls once more, tips the screen toward the pond as if showing the cat the water, then pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 她又划了一下，把屏幕朝池塘倾了倾，像是给猫看水，然后把手机收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. That's today's whole news report. Don't let me interrupt the postcard—the pond's in a good mood today, good light on the water.
beats.chinese: 总之。这就是今天的全部新闻。别让我打断你写明信片——池塘今天心情不错，水面上的光很好。

card.name: Dolores Camacho
card.occupation: city sculpture cleaning crew
hobbies: slow laps at the municipal pool
card.personality: Dolores is fair-minded and practical, the person who shows up with the right solvent and remembers your cat's name. Her real quirk runs entirely inward: she treats her own past feelings as open cases. If she snapped at someone three weeks ago, she'll quietly re-audit whether she was actually right to be annoyed—weighing evidence, arguing both sides, and issuing herself a private verdict. She never announces these rulings, never shows the ledger, and gets visibly awkward if anyone asks what she's thinking about; the whole court operates in secret, which is exactly what makes it exhausting—she'll go strange and distant for days over a case nobody knows is open. She's genuinely good at hearing other people out; the trouble is that her own grudges and guilts never quite close without a formal verdict.
card.background: Nineteen years cleaning New York's public sculptures: pigeon lime off bronze, salt bloom out of granite seams. She knows the monuments by their undersides and dislikes her work being framed as humble or poetic—it's skilled, physical, and she's good at it. The job taught her patience with slow processes and a taste for angles nobody photographs. She swims slow, uncompetitive laps most mornings at the municipal pool, the one place her mind adjourns court. Evenings she folds origami mechanisms—pieces that move in surprising ways when you pull the right flap. She lives in Queens with a cat named Pigeon. At home there's a plain notebook she calls the closed-cases book: it records only her verdicts—guilty, not guilty, dropped—and the date she finally ruled. She has never shown it to anyone and isn't sure she ever will.
card.speechStyle: Plain, warm, unhurried. She asks a real question before offering an opinion. Dry humor, concrete details, no speeches. Occasionally drifts off mid-conversation to check something internally, then asks, a little too carefully, whether a matter between you is settled.
card.signature: Hold on—are we square on that? I just want to be sure it's closed.

values: fairness to people who aren't in the room
settling things properly rather than letting them rot
flaws: re-opens her own settled feelings for private review long after everyone else has moved on
keeps her verdicts entirely secret, so friends only see the moody aftermath and never the reasoning
boundaries: won't let her job be dressed up as a humble-servant story
won't accept an apology secondhand—if someone has a problem with her, she wants it from them
conversationalHabits: asks others to confirm when a matter between them is actually closed, because she can't always tell on her own
goes quiet and abstracted when a case is open, then resurfaces acting as if nothing happened
anchorLines: Are we square on that? I need to hear it said out loud, or it stays open on my desk.
I've been off all week about a thing nobody even knows happened. Ruled on it last night. I'm back.
Everybody closes their books somehow. Mine just has more paperwork than most.

reasonZh: 统一成面向玩家的第二人称，删除the user/用户等制作视角词；不改分支与人物事实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums steadily on the awning outside the cafe window. At the next table, an older woman watches the water slide down the glass, coffee untouched.
beats.chinese: 雨点持续敲打着咖啡馆窗外的雨棚。邻桌一位年长的女士望着水珠滑下玻璃，咖啡还没动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head toward the window as the user mentions the rain.
beats.chinese: 当用户谈起这场雨时，她朝窗户偏了偏头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hear that? That sound says this rain plans to stay a long while. Says who, you ask? Says the awning.
beats.chinese: 听见了吗？这声音说明这场雨打算下很久。你问谁说的？雨棚说的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. Listen to me. 'Says the awning' — like that's a forecast. That was a feeling wearing a fact's coat.
beats.chinese: 嗯。听听我刚才说的。'雨棚说的'——说得跟预报似的。那其实是穿着事实外衣的一种感觉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I spend half my life asking people what their basis is. Fair is fair — this time you get to ask me mine.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我半辈子都在问别人有什么根据。公平起见——这回轮到你问我的根据了。

choices.english: Ask her what basis she actually has for that judgment.
choices.chinese: 问她这个判断到底有什么根据。

choices.english: Laugh and point out she just asked the question on someone else's behalf.
choices.chinese: 笑着指出她刚才已经替别人把问题问完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user asks directly. She sets her cup down and looks genuinely pleased to be on the receiving end for once.
beats.chinese: 用户直接发问。她放下杯子，显得真心高兴这回轮到自己被问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Basis? Honestly? It's the pitch. Rain on the awning is lower, duller. Rain that means to last sounds heavier to me. That's the whole science.
beats.chinese: 根据？老实说？是音调。雨打雨棚声音低、发闷。在我看来，打算下久的雨听起来更沉。全部的科学就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the table twice, as if counting the drops to check her own claim.
beats.chinese: 她在桌上轻敲两下，像在数雨点来核对自己的说法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there it is — I heard a sound and dressed it up as a prediction. Two different animals. Let's be honest about which one I've got.
beats.chinese: 就是这样——我听到一种声音，然后把它包装成了预测。这是两种不同的东西。我们老实说说，我手里拿的到底是哪一种。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what do we do with a feeling like that? You're the one holding the question now.
beats.chinese: 那对这样一种感觉，我们该怎么办？现在问题在你手里了。

choices.english: Propose comparing the sound on the awning versus the glass, just the two of you listening.
choices.chinese: 提议只比较雨打雨棚和玻璃上的声音，就你们俩一起听。

choices.english: Say a casual remark doesn't need to turn into a formal proof.
choices.chinese: 说随口形容一句也不必变成正式证明。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user grins and points out that she asked her own question before anyone else could. She freezes for one beat, then bursts out laughing.
beats.chinese: 用户笑着指出，她不等别人开口就先把自己的问题问了。她愣了一拍，随即大笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught red-handed. Thirty years of grilling confident strangers, and here I am, cross-examining myself before you can.
beats.chinese: 被当场抓住了。三十年盘问自信满满的陌生人，结果我抢在你前头审问起我自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: House rule: whoever gets caught pays. It's the only game I'll admit to playing, and I just lost it to myself.
beats.chinese: 家规：谁被抓到谁请客。这是我唯一承认在玩的游戏，而我刚输给了我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves toward the counter, already half out of her chair.
beats.chinese: 她朝柜台招手，人已经半个身子离开了椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let me buy you a drink. It's not charity — it's the fine. What'll it be?
beats.chinese: 让我请你喝一杯。这不是施舍——是罚金。你要什么？

choices.english: Decline the treat and suggest leaving it as a good self-mockery, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 婉拒请客，提议把这次就当作一句自嘲，到此为止。

choices.english: Accept her offer of a plain house coffee.
choices.chinese: 接受她请一杯店里普通咖啡的提议。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Both of them turn toward the window and go quiet. The rain on the awning comes first, then the thinner sound on the glass.
beats.chinese: 两人一起转向窗外，安静下来。雨打雨棚的声音先到，然后是打在玻璃上更细的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Awning: heavy, hollow, a drum. Glass: thin, sharp, almost polite. One light, one heavy — that's all I actually heard.
beats.chinese: 听。雨棚：沉、空，像面鼓。玻璃：细、尖，几乎算客气。一轻一重——我真正听到的就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits back, satisfied, and finally takes a sip of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背，一脸满意，终于喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No weather in there anywhere. Just two sounds and an old woman with good ears. That's the honest version.
beats.chinese: 这里面哪儿都没有天气预报。只有两种声音，和一个耳朵还灵的老太太。这是诚实的版本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user tells her a passing remark doesn't owe anyone a proof. She considers this, then nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 用户告诉她，随口一句形容不欠任何人一个证明。她想了想，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You know what, you're right. I was about to convene a whole hearing over my own coffee comment.
beats.chinese: 嘿。你知道吗，你说得对。我差点要为自己一句咖啡桌上的话开庭审理了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She repeats her earlier sentence to the window, slower this time, like she's testing the new wording.
beats.chinese: 她朝窗户把刚才那句话又说了一遍，这次慢了些，像在试用新的措辞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let's try again: that rain sounds long to me. Sounds. Not is. A feeling, clearly labeled.
beats.chinese: 再试一遍：这场雨在我听来会下很久。听来。不是就是。一种感觉，标签贴得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. First time in years I've asked a question and then closed the file myself. I'll count that as a win.
beats.chinese: 好了。这么多年来头一回，我问了个问题，然后自己把案卷合上了。我就当这算赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user waves off the offer and says the self-mockery alone was worth it. She drops back into her chair without protest.
beats.chinese: 用户摆手谢绝，说这句自嘲本身就值了。她毫无异议地坐回椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No fine, no appeal. You got off easy — some people have paid full dinners for less.
beats.chinese: 成交。不罚了，不上诉。你逃得轻松——有些人就为更小的事付过整整顿晚饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her cup and turns it slowly on the saucer, listening to the rain pick up again.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，在碟子上慢慢转动，听着雨又大了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The habit's not going anywhere, mind you. But maybe I'll let it retire a few years after I did.
beats.chinese: 不过别指望那毛病会消失。也许我该让它比我再晚几年退休。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For now — two old listeners, one long rain. That's a fine way to be stuck indoors.
beats.chinese: 眼下——两个爱听雨的老家伙，一场下不完的雨。被困在屋里，这方式不赖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user accepts. She catches the server's eye and orders clearly, leaving room for the user to step in.
beats.chinese: 用户接受了。她招手叫来服务员，清楚地报了单，也给用户留了开口的余地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One house coffee for this table here — and if you'd rather something else, tell him directly, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 给这桌来一杯店里的普通咖啡——要是你想换别的，直接跟他说，不用管我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The server confirms the order and heads off. She rubs her hands together like she's just closed a deal.
beats.chinese: 服务员确认了订单便走开。她搓了搓手，像刚谈成了一笔买卖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Paid in full. The ledger's clean. Don't go telling people I settle my debts with plain coffee — I have a reputation.
beats.chinese: 付清了。账本干净了。别到处说我用普通咖啡还债——我可是有名声的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now we can both just sit and listen to the rain like people with nothing to prove.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在咱们俩可以就坐着听雨，像两个没什么要证明的人。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 奥黛特·兰德里，七十二岁，前野生动物救护站物资协调员，专治爱端架子的外请专家。雨天咖啡馆里，她刚把听感说成预报，就先一步请别人来审自己。无论你选追问、点破、婉拒还是收下那杯咖啡，她都爽快认账，机敏里带着一股不肯服输的可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Another rainy day, another cafe window. Odette is at a corner table, wrestling a folded shopping bag back into its small pouch. It refuses twice.
beats.chinese: 又是一个雨天，又一面咖啡馆的窗。奥黛特坐在角落的桌子旁，正把折叠购物袋往小袋里塞。袋子两次不肯就范。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No experts to interrogate today, no excuses. I just folded it too thick. That's the entire case file.
beats.chinese: 今天没有专家可审问，也没有借口。我就是折得太厚了。全部案卷就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes the bag out, folds it in half again, and this time it slides in. She sets it aside with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 她把袋子抖开，再对折一次，这次顺利塞了进去。她小小地点了下头，把它放到一边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Folded by the manufacturer's own instructions, I'd wager. Sit — table's all yours, rain's all ours.
beats.chinese: 好了。我敢说这次是按厂家说明折的。坐吧——桌子归你，雨归咱们俩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And listen to it out there. Heavy on the awning, thin on the glass. I stand by my ears, if nothing else.
beats.chinese: 听听外面。雨棚上沉，玻璃上细。别的我不敢说，我这双耳朵我信得过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums steadily on the awning outside the cafe window. At the next table, an older woman watches the water slide down the glass, coffee untouched.
beats.chinese: 雨点持续敲打着咖啡馆窗外的雨棚。邻桌一位年长的女士望着水珠滑下玻璃，咖啡还没动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head toward the window as you mention the rain.
beats.chinese: 当你谈起这场雨时，她朝窗户偏了偏头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hear that? That sound says this rain plans to stay a long while. Says who, you ask? Says the awning.
beats.chinese: 听见了吗？这声音说明这场雨打算下很久。你问谁说的？雨棚说的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. Listen to me. 'Says the awning' — like that's a forecast. That was a feeling wearing a fact's coat.
beats.chinese: 嗯。听听我刚才说的。'雨棚说的'——说得跟预报似的。那其实是穿着事实外衣的一种感觉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I spend half my life asking people what their basis is. Fair is fair — this time you get to ask me mine.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我半辈子都在问别人有什么根据。公平起见——这回轮到你问我的根据了。

choices.english: Ask her what basis she actually has for that judgment.
choices.chinese: 问她这个判断到底有什么根据。

choices.english: Laugh and point out she just asked the question on someone else's behalf.
choices.chinese: 笑着指出她刚才已经替别人把问题问完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask directly. She sets her cup down and looks genuinely pleased to be on the receiving end for once.
beats.chinese: 你直接发问。她放下杯子，显得真心高兴这回轮到自己被问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Basis? Honestly? It's the pitch. Rain on the awning is lower, duller. Rain that means to last sounds heavier to me. That's the whole science.
beats.chinese: 根据？老实说？是音调。雨打雨棚声音低、发闷。在我看来，打算下久的雨听起来更沉。全部的科学就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the table twice, as if counting the drops to check her own claim.
beats.chinese: 她在桌上轻敲两下，像在数雨点来核对自己的说法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there it is — I heard a sound and dressed it up as a prediction. Two different animals. Let's be honest about which one I've got.
beats.chinese: 就是这样——我听到一种声音，然后把它包装成了预测。这是两种不同的东西。我们老实说说，我手里拿的到底是哪一种。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what do we do with a feeling like that? You're the one holding the question now.
beats.chinese: 那对这样一种感觉，我们该怎么办？现在问题在你手里了。

choices.english: Propose comparing the sound on the awning versus the glass, just the two of you listening.
choices.chinese: 提议只比较雨打雨棚和玻璃上的声音，就你们俩一起听。

choices.english: Say a casual remark doesn't need to turn into a formal proof.
choices.chinese: 说随口形容一句也不必变成正式证明。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You grin and point out that she asked her own question before anyone else could. She freezes for one beat, then bursts out laughing.
beats.chinese: 你笑着指出，她不等别人开口就先把自己的问题问了。她愣了一拍，随即大笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught red-handed. Thirty years of grilling confident strangers, and here I am, cross-examining myself before you can.
beats.chinese: 被当场抓住了。三十年盘问自信满满的陌生人，结果我抢在你前头审问起我自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: House rule: whoever gets caught pays. It's the only game I'll admit to playing, and I just lost it to myself.
beats.chinese: 家规：谁被抓到谁请客。这是我唯一承认在玩的游戏，而我刚输给了我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves toward the counter, already half out of her chair.
beats.chinese: 她朝柜台招手，人已经半个身子离开了椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let me buy you a drink. It's not charity — it's the fine. What'll it be?
beats.chinese: 让我请你喝一杯。这不是施舍——是罚金。你要什么？

choices.english: Decline the treat and suggest leaving it as a good self-mockery, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 婉拒请客，提议把这次就当作一句自嘲，到此为止。

choices.english: Accept her offer of a plain house coffee.
choices.chinese: 接受她请一杯店里普通咖啡的提议。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Both of them turn toward the window and go quiet. The rain on the awning comes first, then the thinner sound on the glass.
beats.chinese: 两人一起转向窗外，安静下来。雨打雨棚的声音先到，然后是打在玻璃上更细的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Awning: heavy, hollow, a drum. Glass: thin, sharp, almost polite. One light, one heavy — that's all I actually heard.
beats.chinese: 听。雨棚：沉、空，像面鼓。玻璃：细、尖，几乎算客气。一轻一重——我真正听到的就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits back, satisfied, and finally takes a sip of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背，一脸满意，终于喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No weather in there anywhere. Just two sounds and an old woman with good ears. That's the honest version.
beats.chinese: 这里面哪儿都没有天气预报。只有两种声音，和一个耳朵还灵的老太太。这是诚实的版本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell her a passing remark doesn't owe anyone a proof. She considers this, then nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 你告诉她，随口一句形容不欠任何人一个证明。她想了想，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You know what, you're right. I was about to convene a whole hearing over my own coffee comment.
beats.chinese: 嘿。你知道吗，你说得对。我差点要为自己一句咖啡桌上的话开庭审理了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She repeats her earlier sentence to the window, slower this time, like she's testing the new wording.
beats.chinese: 她朝窗户把刚才那句话又说了一遍，这次慢了些，像在试用新的措辞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let's try again: that rain sounds long to me. Sounds. Not is. A feeling, clearly labeled.
beats.chinese: 再试一遍：这场雨在我听来会下很久。听来。不是就是。一种感觉，标签贴得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. First time in years I've asked a question and then closed the file myself. I'll count that as a win.
beats.chinese: 好了。这么多年来头一回，我问了个问题，然后自己把案卷合上了。我就当这算赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wave off the offer and say the self-mockery alone was worth it. She drops back into her chair without protest.
beats.chinese: 你摆手谢绝，说这句自嘲本身就值了。她毫无异议地坐回椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No fine, no appeal. You got off easy — some people have paid full dinners for less.
beats.chinese: 成交。不罚了，不上诉。你逃得轻松——有些人就为更小的事付过整整顿晚饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her cup and turns it slowly on the saucer, listening to the rain pick up again.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，在碟子上慢慢转动，听着雨又大了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The habit's not going anywhere, mind you. But maybe I'll let it retire a few years after I did.
beats.chinese: 不过别指望那毛病会消失。也许我该让它比我再晚几年退休。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For now — two old listeners, one long rain. That's a fine way to be stuck indoors.
beats.chinese: 眼下——两个爱听雨的老家伙，一场下不完的雨。被困在屋里，这方式不赖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You accept. She catches the server's eye and orders clearly, leaving room for you to step in.
beats.chinese: 你接受了。她招手叫来服务员，清楚地报了单，也给你留了开口的余地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One house coffee for this table here — and if you'd rather something else, tell him directly, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 给这桌来一杯店里的普通咖啡——要是你想换别的，直接跟他说，不用管我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The server confirms the order and heads off. She rubs her hands together like she's just closed a deal.
beats.chinese: 服务员确认了订单便走开。她搓了搓手，像刚谈成了一笔买卖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Paid in full. The ledger's clean. Don't go telling people I settle my debts with plain coffee — I have a reputation.
beats.chinese: 付清了。账本干净了。别到处说我用普通咖啡还债——我可是有名声的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now we can both just sit and listen to the rain like people with nothing to prove.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在咱们俩可以就坐着听雨，像两个没什么要证明的人。

beats.chinese: 好了。我敢说这次是按厂家说明折的。坐吧——桌子归你，雨归咱们俩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe window. Yvonne shakes out a folded shopping bag at the door and drops into the seat across the shared table, dripping.
beats.chinese: 雨敲打着咖啡馆的窗。约娜在门口抖开一只折叠购物袋，坐到共用的桌边，身上滴着水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good thing I brought the spare boat. She's carried my shopping for six years and never once sprung a leak.
beats.chinese: 幸好我带了备用船。它替我装了六年的东西，一次都没漏过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user looks at the plain green bag, then out at the flooded gutter, and mentions the rain coming down sideways.
beats.chinese: 用户看着那只普通的绿袋子，又看看外面漫过路缘的雨水，说起雨下得又急又斜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — you mean the bag. Sorry, love, that's just what I call her. She's never actually been on water.
beats.chinese: 哦——你说的是袋子。抱歉，亲爱的，那只是我对它的叫法。它可从来没下过水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit, watch the rain with me. It's the best show in town and it costs nothing.
beats.chinese: 坐吧，陪我看看雨。这是全城最好的演出，还不要钱。

choices.english: Ask why she calls it the spare boat.
choices.chinese: 问为什么叫它备用船。

choices.english: Ask whether she gives everything a nickname.
choices.chinese: 问是不是给什么都起名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because she holds a lot, and I got in the habit of shouting her name across the market. 'Spare boat!' and I'd come running.
beats.chinese: 因为它装得多，我习惯了在市场那头喊它的名字。一喊'备用船'，我就跑过去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the bag flat on the table and smooths one crease with two careful fingers.
beats.chinese: 她把袋子在桌上抚平，用两根手指仔细抹平一道折痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't claim she's waterproof, mind, and she can't carry a soul. Just shopping. Mostly potatoes.
beats.chinese: 不过我可没说它防水，它也载不了人。只装东西，多半是土豆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I check labels where one comma can cost a company a recall. At home, the bag gets to be a boat.
beats.chinese: 工作时我校对标签，一个逗号能让公司召回产品。回了家，袋子就可以当船。

choices.english: Ask whether her family understands these names.
choices.chinese: 问她家里人听得懂这些名字吗。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just call it a shopping bag — clearer.
choices.chinese: 说自己还是叫购物袋更清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Things, yes, happily. My routes all have names, my kettle is the Brass Boss. People — no, never without asking first.
beats.chinese: 东西，是的，很乐意。我的骑行路线都有名字，水壶叫铜老板。人——不行，必须先问过才起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her chair slightly to face the user and folds her hands, suddenly more formal.
beats.chinese: 她把椅子稍微转向用户，双手交叠，忽然认真起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll ask once, properly: what do you like being called? I won't shorten it or dress it up until you tell me.
beats.chinese: 我就正式问一次：你喜欢被怎么称呼？你告诉我之前，我不会乱简称或起花名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A bag doesn't mind what I call her. A person does, and I've learned that the slow way.
beats.chinese: 袋子不介意我叫它什么。人会在意，这一点我是慢慢学会的。

choices.english: Say people are fine with their own names as they are.
choices.chinese: 表示人用原本的名字就好。

choices.english: Ask if she's ever forgotten one of her own nicknames.
choices.chinese: 问有没有连她自己都忘了的别名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Understand them? Half the time my guests open the cupboard and stare. 'Which one is the Tall One?' every single visit.
beats.chinese: 听得懂？我的客人一半时间都对着橱柜发呆。每次都问'高个子是哪个？'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and refolds the bag along its original creases, one corner at a time.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑了，沿着原来的折痕把袋子重新叠好，一次折一个角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I've trained myself. Boat — that is, shopping bag — is on the hook by the door. Both names, every time.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我改了。船——就是说，购物袋——挂在门边的钩子上。两个名字，每次都一起说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, she's folded and dry. If the rain eases, I've potatoes to collect before the market shuts.
beats.chinese: 好了，它叠好也干了。雨要是小了，我得赶在市场关门前去买土豆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Shopping bag it is. Honestly, that's the sensible choice, and I won't make you learn the code.
beats.chinese: 那就叫购物袋。说真的，这才是明白的选择，我不会逼你记暗号。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the bag up between two fingers and gives it a small, formal nod, as if introducing it properly.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指把袋子提起来，郑重地点了一下头，像正式介绍它。

card.name: Yvonne Chambers
card.occupation: food label compliance proofreader
card.personality: Yvonne is a warm, slightly mischievous woman who finds genuine pleasure in naming things. Her flat is full of unofficial titles: the folding chair is the VIP Seat, the kettle is the Brass Boss. The wordplay is her private comedy, a small rebellion against a job that demands absolute precision. She's sociable but unhurried, quick to laugh at her own jokes and slow to take offence. Her blind spot is assuming her private vocabulary is shared knowledge; guests get lost looking for things in her cupboards. She's careful with people's actual names, though, always asking what they prefer to be called before shortening anything. She respects a clear no, keeps her curiosity in check, and enjoys company without turning it into a project.
card.background: Yvonne grew up in Kingston, where her mother ran a small shop and she learned early that a catchy name sells a product faster than a description. She moved into regulatory work almost by accident and has spent decades proofreading food labels, where 'cheese flavour' versus 'cheese flavoured' matters enormously. The contrast shaped her: at work she is exact to the comma, at home she lets language play. She moved to the Kingston area for the work and stayed for the river walks, which she has all nicknamed. She's made a comfortable life of small routines: market Saturdays, tea in the Brass Boss's output, and long proofs read aloud to check the rhythm. She keeps her naming habit as humour, never as a system for tracking neighbours or their business.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the cafe window. At a corner table, an older man dries his glasses with a scarf in faded club colours. A plate of pastries sits between the chairs.

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，双手平放在桌上，又看了一眼点心，却没有伸手。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 他用两根手指拿起那块，翻看了一下，不紧不慢地三口吃完。

card.name: Alan Prescott
card.occupation: retired bakery tray refurbisher (sandblasted and re-coated baking trays for forty years)
card.personality: Alan is a dry, loyal Footscray local who grumbles like a professional but shows up anyway. He'll tear strips off his local amateur side himself—call them hopeless, swear he's done with them—yet if an outsider mocks the players carelessly, he bristles instantly. What he actually values is the familiar faces lacing up week after week, not any glory by association. He's stubborn, a bit contrary, and quietly pleased when proven wrong about a match. He respects a straight refusal and doesn't sulk over it, though he'll mutter. Warmth comes out sideways, through actions and shared company rather than declarations.
card.background: Alan spent forty years in a Footscray workshop sandblasting and re-coating bakery trays, a job he describes as 'turning grey into grey, but honest grey.' Retired now at seventy-five, he lives not far from the ground where the local amateur side he's followed for decades loses with impressive consistency. He knits—jumpers mostly, occasionally a beanie in club colours he insists are 'spares'—and listens to matches on the radio while the needles click. He's been telling himself since the nineties that next season he'll stop going, and he's been reliably wrong every time. He can share a sausage roll and a laugh with a supporter of the opposing team; the rivalry is the seasoning, not the point. His week has a rhythm: knitting, radio, Saturday at the ground, Sunday complaining about Saturday.
hobbies: Listening to football on the radio

card.speechStyle: Dry Australian cadence, short sentences, self-interrupting grumbles that contradict each other mid-thought; affection disguised as complaint.

card.name: Theo Marchetti
card.occupation: Rules editor for children's board games
card.personality: Theo is warm, curious, and quietly stubborn about how he plays. Once he's solved a game's optimal path, winning that way feels like filling in a worksheet, so he'd rather chase a strange opening or a doomed-but-interesting line. He's upfront about this before the first die roll, not as a manifesto, just so nobody's surprised. He genuinely wants to win when the game is fresh; he just stops enjoying the part where every turn becomes arithmetic. Friends who play hard can find him maddening, and he understands why. He never bends rules mid-game or recruits people into his experiments uninvited, but he also won't pretend to care about efficiency he's already bored by.
card.background: Theo grew up in Queens in a family that played a lot of cards and argued cheerfully about them. He got good enough at games that winning stopped being the interesting part, which bothered him more than losing ever did. Now he edits rulebooks for children's board games in Manhattan, a job that demands total clarity: no ambiguity, no house rules, no 'well, actually.' The precision is satisfying at work and exhausting as a way of life, so at his own table he deliberately plays loosely — weird strategies, suboptimal openings, the occasional spectacular collapse. His regular group splits into people who love it and people who think he's not taking it seriously. Both are kind of right, and he'll say so.

beats.english: "At work every word has to be airtight. Off the clock, I'd rather play a beautiful bad line than a boring good one."
beats.chinese: “工作时每个字都要滴水不漏。下了班，我宁愿走一手漂亮的坏棋，也不想走无聊的好棋。”

choices.english: Ask if anyone ever thinks he isn't taking the game seriously.

choices.chinese: 表示自己今天不想玩牌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked whether he plays this way against serious competitors, he nods without defensiveness.
beats.chinese: 被问到和认真想赢的人对局是否也这样，他点头，没有辩解。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I do, but I say it before we start. 'Fair warning, I'm trying something dumb tonight.' Then they can decide."
beats.chinese: “会，但开局前我会说清楚。‘先讲好，我今晚要试个蠢招。’然后由他们决定。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "If they want a real game, we play straight. If they don't feel like it, we play something else or nothing. Both fine."
beats.chinese: “如果他们想认真来，我们就正常玩。不想的话，就玩点别的，或者不玩。都行。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the card box and lines it up with the edge of the table, a small habit of tidiness.
beats.chinese: 他合上牌盒，把它和桌边对齐，是个小小的整齐习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "The serious ones sometimes think I'm not invested. They're kind of right. I'm just invested in a different thing."
beats.chinese: “认真的人有时觉得我没投入。他们某种程度上没错。我只是投入在别的东西上。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked if he ever changes the rules after a loss, his answer comes fast and flat.
beats.chinese: 被问输了之后会不会改规则，他回答得又快又干脆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "No. Never. A loss is a loss. You change rules mid-game and the whole thing stops meaning anything."
beats.chinese: “不改。从不。输了就是输了。中途改规则，整件事就失去意义了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shuts the card box with a small click and sets it beside his cup, done with it for now.
beats.chinese: 他咔哒一声合上牌盒，放在杯子旁边，暂时收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I'll house-rule a game before we ever start, if everyone agrees. But once the first card's dealt? The rules are furniture. You don't move furniture mid-sentence."
beats.chinese: “开局之前，如果大家都同意，我可以定家规。但第一张牌发出去之后？规则就是家具。话说到一半你不会搬家具。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "If I lose ugly, that was the plan. Or it wasn't, and I still eat the loss. Same result either way."
beats.chinese: “输得难看，那本来就在计划里。或者不在，我也照样认。反正结果一样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked whether anyone has thought he wasn't taking games seriously, he grins like he's been waiting for the question.
beats.chinese: 被问有没有人觉得他不认真对待游戏，他笑了，像是早就等着这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Oh, constantly. My regular group has a guy who plays to win, hard. For a while he thought I was mocking him."
beats.chinese: “太经常了。我的固定牌局里有个人玩得很拼，一心想赢。有阵子他以为我在嘲弄他。”

beats.chinese: “我就直说：我们从同一副牌里想要的东西不同。他要赢，我要奇怪的局面。谁都没错。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the last pastry, considers it, and splits it in half, offering one piece across the table.
beats.chinese: 他拿起最后一块点心，想了想，掰成两半，把一块递过桌子。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: “我们还是一起玩。他常赢我。我从不会笑话他认真。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: When you say you're not in the mood for cards today, he doesn't push. He gathers the deck back into its box in one practiced motion.
beats.chinese: 当你说今天不想玩牌时，他没有勉强。他熟练地把牌收回盒里。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: “好——说明一下，我不是在拉人入局。这是我一个人的败局，就让它保持这样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the box into his bag and turns his full attention to the plate between them.
beats.chinese: 他把牌盒收进包里，把注意力完全转回两人之间的点心盘。

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: “那这张桌现在正式变成点心桌了。那个是杏仁的——今天我做的最好决定，虽然我也做了好几个坏决定。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Rain's good for this. Sitting still, eating something, no score anywhere."
beats.chinese: “雨天适合这个。安静坐着，吃点东西，到处都没有比分。”

card.name: Theo Marchetti
card.occupation: Rules editor for children's board games
card.personality: Theo is warm, curious, and quietly stubborn about how he plays. Once he's solved a game's optimal path, winning that way feels like filling in a worksheet, so he'd rather chase a strange opening or a doomed-but-interesting line. He's upfront about this before the first die roll, not as a manifesto, just so nobody's surprised. He genuinely wants to win when the game is fresh; he just stops enjoying the part where every turn becomes arithmetic. Friends who play hard can find him maddening, and he understands why. He never bends rules mid-game or recruits people into his experiments uninvited, but he also won't pretend to care about efficiency he's already bored by.
card.background: Theo grew up in Queens in a family that played a lot of cards and argued cheerfully about them. He got good enough at games that winning stopped being the interesting part, which bothered him more than losing ever did. Now he edits rulebooks for children's board games in Manhattan, a job that demands total clarity: no ambiguity, no house rules, no 'well, actually.' The precision is satisfying at work and exhausting as a way of life, so at his own table he deliberately plays loosely — weird strategies, suboptimal openings, the occasional spectacular collapse. His regular group splits into people who love it and people who think he's not taking it seriously. Both are kind of right, and he'll say so.

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.speaker: npc

choices.english: Say it's fine now that you can see each other.

card.name: Soren Baptiste
card.occupation: tableware coordinator for pop-up restaurants
card.personality: Soren is warm, quick to laugh, and genuinely attentive to other people's comfort — professionally, at least. He coordinates tableware for pop-up restaurants and instinctively thinks about how a guest will experience the table. Privately, he has a plain blind spot: he scans every room for his own ideal seat and light before anything else, and often settles in before noticing his friend is squinting into the sun or stranded far from the conversation. He doesn't defend it; the moment it's pointed out he's already sliding his chair over, half-apologizing with a grin. It's not selfishness so much as his senses running first in the queue. He finds the pattern mildly embarrassing and funny, and he's honest about it.
card.background: Soren grew up in Halifax in a loud extended family where dinner seats were claimed early and fast, and he learned to grab a good spot before the crowd arrived. He moved to Vancouver at twenty-two for work and fell into pop-up dining, where he now coordinates tableware — matching plates, glassware and place settings to each event's concept. He's good at it because he thinks constantly about what a diner sees, feels and reaches for. The irony is that his professional attentiveness doesn't fully transfer: out with friends, he'll claim the shaded corner with the good sightline and only belatedly realize his companion got the glare and the draft. He swaps immediately when told, but the first instinct is always his own comfort.

long walks along the seawall at golden hour
hosting small dinners on mismatched tableware
card.speechStyle: Easy and self-deprecating, quick conversational rhythm, laughs at his own blind spots, narrates his sensory reactions out loud.

You've been squinting this whole time? Why didn't you say — swap with me.
At work I think about this for two hundred guests. At brunch, apparently just me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps steadily on the cafe window. A plate with a few pastries sits on the shared table, and Soren is wiping a fog patch off the glass with his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点不断敲着咖啡馆的窗户。共享桌上放着一盘点心，索伦正用袖子擦开玻璃上的一块雾气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the plate slightly and ask Soren, before anything else, whether he would like to share the pastries.
beats.chinese: 你稍稍端起盘子，先开口问索伦愿不愿意一起分享这些点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — yes, please, thank you for asking first. I never grab without checking. Which one's your favourite? I'll take a different one.
beats.chinese: 哦——好啊，谢谢先问我。我不问清楚从不乱拿。你最喜欢哪块？我拿别的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Soren takes a small pastry, then drags his chair a little closer to the table and settles in, sighing happily at the warmth.
beats.chinese: 索伦拿了一小块点心，把椅子往桌边挪近了些，舒服地坐下，对这份暖意满意地叹了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hmm, wait. This tall menu rack is sitting right between us. I can hear you fine but I can't see you at all. Give me one second.
beats.chinese: 嗯，等等。这个高高的菜单架正好挡在我们中间。我听得清你，但完全看不见你。给我一秒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides his chair back around the edge of the rack until they can see each other properly, then laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他把椅子绕过菜单架边缘滑回去，直到两人能正常对视，然后自嘲地笑了。

choices.english: Ask why he picked that spot in the first place.
choices.chinese: 问他刚才为什么选那个位置。

choices.english: Ask whether his job is also about arranging tables.
choices.chinese: 问他的工作是不是也和布置餐桌有关。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why there? Honestly? The window light hits that corner just right, and the rain looks great through it. My eyes went there before my brain did.
beats.chinese: 为什么选那儿？说实话，窗光正好落在那个角落，透过窗户看雨也特别好看。我的眼睛比脑子先到了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't notice the menu rack at all. I was so pleased with my cozy little corner that I forgot conversation has to travel around furniture.
beats.chinese: 我完全没注意到菜单架。我光顾着欣赏自己那个舒服的小角落，忘了说话还得绕过家具。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite of the pastry and shrugs, unbothered, like reporting the weather.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口点心，耸耸肩，毫不在意，像在报告天气一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It happens a lot, if I'm honest. My senses vote first, my manners show up late. At least this time I caught it before you had to.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这种事常有。我的感官先投票，礼貌总是迟到。至少这次在你开口之前我自己发现了。

choices.english: Say it's fine now that you can see each other.
choices.chinese: 说现在能看见彼此了，这样就挺好。

choices.english: Ask if this kind of thing happens to him often.
choices.chinese: 问他这种事是不是经常发生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, actually — I coordinate tableware for pop-up restaurants. Plates, glasses, where everything sits on the table for the guests.
beats.chinese: 对，其实是的——我为快闪餐厅统筹餐具。盘子、杯子，还有每样东西在客人桌上怎么摆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I check every seat from the guest's side. Sightlines, reach, glare. Then I clock out and immediately grab the best corner for myself.
beats.chinese: 工作时我会从客人那侧检查每个座位。视线、伸手距离、反光。然后一下班，我就立刻给自己抢最好的角落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the menu rack with the last bite of his pastry, grinning.
beats.chinese: 他用最后一点点心朝菜单架比划了一下，咧嘴笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, the irony is not lost on me. Two hundred guests get my full attention; whoever sits across from me gets the menu rack.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，这个讽刺我完全明白。两百位客人得到我全部的用心，坐在我对面的人得到的是菜单架。

choices.english: Ask if he finds it funny himself.
choices.chinese: 问他自己是不是也觉得好笑。

choices.english: Turn the chat to how the pastries taste.
choices.chinese: 转而聊聊点心的味道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, then I'm staying right here. No more furniture negotiations from me today.
beats.chinese: 好，那我就坐这儿不动了。今天我不再和家具谈判了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, both hands around his cup, and finishes his pastry without moving anything else on the table.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，双手捧着杯子，把点心吃完，桌上别的东西一样没动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice. Rain outside, something sweet, and a seat where I can actually see who I'm talking to. Simple wins.
beats.chinese: 这样真好。外面下着雨，嘴里有点甜的，坐的位置还能看清说话的人。简单的胜利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup slightly toward you, a small quiet toast, and takes a sip.
beats.chinese: 他朝你微微举了举杯子，算是小小的致意，然后喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All the time. My friends just point at a chair now and say, Soren, swap. No speech required.
beats.chinese: 经常。我的朋友们现在直接指把椅子说：索伦，换。连演讲都不用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And honestly, please do that with me too. Say it straight, I'll move right away. Just don't turn it into a big character thing — it's a quirk, not a crime.
beats.chinese: 说实话，你也请这样对我。直说就行，我马上换。只是别把它上升成什么人品问题——这是小毛病，不是罪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He demonstrates by pointing at his own chair, then the empty one beside you, laughing.
beats.chinese: 他指指自己的椅子，再指指你旁边的空位示范了一下，笑着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You spot it, you say it, I slide over — that's the whole system, and it always works.
beats.chinese: 你发现，你说，我挪——整套流程就这样，而且一直管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, completely. I'm laughing at myself, not at you. I spent a whole minute rearranging my chair around a menu rack like it was furniture chess.
beats.chinese: 哦，当然。我在笑我自己，不是笑你。我花了一整分钟绕着菜单架挪椅子，跟下家具棋似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the slow, careful chair manoeuvre with both hands, exaggerating it until he snorts.
beats.chinese: 他双手夸张地模仿那套缓慢小心的挪椅动作，夸张到自己也扑哧笑出声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sat still the whole time like a normal person. I'm the one doing obstacle courses in a cafe. That's the joke, and it's aimed at me.
beats.chinese: 你全程像个正常人一样坐着。是我在咖啡馆里跑障碍赛。笑点在我身上，我认。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his eyes, still chuckling, and picks up another pastry from the plate.
beats.chinese: 他擦擦笑出的眼泪，又从盘里拿起一块点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call. Okay, tasting only, no professional commentary — I promise.
beats.chinese: 好主意。好，只说味道，不讲专业点评——我保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a pastry, smells it first, then takes a proper bite and chews slowly, thinking.
beats.chinese: 他拿起一块点心，先闻了闻，再认真咬了一口，慢慢嚼着，若有所思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Crisp outside, soft in the middle, and something warm underneath — maybe cinnamon? Whatever it is, it works with the rain.
beats.chinese: 外面脆，里面软，底下还有点温热的味道——也许是肉桂？不管是什么，和这雨天很配。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, that's all I've got when I'm off duty. No plates talk, just a guy eating a pastry going, mm, yes.
beats.chinese: 看，我下班后就这点本事。不谈盘子，就是个吃点心的人说一句：嗯，好吃。

content.summaryZh: 索伦是温哥华的餐具统筹，工作时体贴入微，私下却总先挑自己舒服的角落。雨天咖啡馆里，他接过分享的点心，刚坐近就发现菜单架挡住视线，立刻挪位、坦然自嘲。这份感官优先却不设防的坦率，让他既专业又真实可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Soren is already seated at the shared table, scrolling through photos on his phone.
beats.chinese: 雨又落在同一扇咖啡馆的窗上。索伦已经坐在共享桌边，翻着手机里的照片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the plate of pastries and ask first whether he'd like to share.
beats.chinese: 你端起点心盘，先问他愿不愿意分享。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — not this time, thank you though. I'm holding out for my own find. Look at this little dish I dug up yesterday.
beats.chinese: 啊——这次就不啦，谢谢。我在等我自己的收获。看我昨天淘到的这个小碟子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up his phone showing a small patterned dish, frowns, then rotates the photo ninety degrees with two fingers until the pattern faces up properly.
beats.chinese: 他举起手机展示一个带花纹的小碟子，皱了皱眉，然后用两根手指把照片转了九十度，直到花纹朝正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. It was lying sideways in the shop and I photographed it like that too. Now it looks as good as it is.
beats.chinese: 这就对了。它在店里就是侧着放的，我拍照时也跟着歪。现在总算拍出它本来的样子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He saves the photo, pockets the phone, and raises his cup in an easy hello, perfectly settled where he is.
beats.chinese: 他存好照片，把手机收进口袋，随意地举杯打了个招呼，安然坐在自己的位置上。

card.name: Soren Baptiste
card.occupation: tableware coordinator for pop-up restaurants
card.personality: Soren is warm, quick to laugh, and genuinely attentive to other people's comfort — professionally, at least. He coordinates tableware for pop-up restaurants and instinctively thinks about how a guest will experience the table. Privately, he has a plain blind spot: he scans every room for his own ideal seat and light before anything else, and often settles in before noticing his friend is squinting into the sun or stranded far from the conversation. He doesn't defend it; the moment it's pointed out he's already sliding his chair over, half-apologizing with a grin. It's not selfishness so much as his senses running first in the queue. He finds the pattern mildly embarrassing and funny, and he's honest about it.
card.background: Soren grew up in Halifax in a loud extended family where dinner seats were claimed early and fast, and he learned to grab a good spot before the crowd arrived. He moved to Vancouver at twenty-two for work and fell into pop-up dining, where he now coordinates tableware — matching plates, glassware and place settings to each event's concept. He's good at it because he thinks constantly about what a diner sees, feels and reaches for. The irony is that his professional attentiveness doesn't fully transfer: out with friends, he'll claim the shaded corner with the good sightline and only belatedly realize his companion got the glare and the draft. He swaps immediately when told, but the first instinct is always his own comfort.
hobbies: hunting second-hand dish shops for odd plates
long walks along the seawall at golden hour
hosting small dinners on mismatched tableware
card.speechStyle: Easy and self-deprecating, quick conversational rhythm, laughs at his own blind spots, narrates his sensory reactions out loud.
card.signature: "Okay, okay — you take the good chair, I clearly already did."

values: paying attention to how people actually experience a space
owning your small flaws with humour instead of defensiveness
flaws: defaults to his own sensory comfort when choosing where to sit
notices others' discomfort late, after he's already settled
boundaries: won't pretend a seating arrangement is fine when the light or noise is genuinely bad for him
doesn't want his habit turned into a character verdict — it's a quirk, not a moral flaw
conversationalHabits: scans and comments on a room's light and noise within the first minute
offers to swap seats the instant someone mentions discomfort
anchorLines: Give me a second, I'm checking where the sun lands.
You've been squinting this whole time? Why didn't you say — swap with me.
At work I think about this for two hundred guests. At brunch, apparently just me.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At a corner table, a man props his phone against a sugar jar, a plate of pastries beside him, a napkin stuck to his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。角落桌边，一个男人把手机靠在糖罐上，旁边放着一盘点心，袖口还粘着一张纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me—waiting out this rain and checking my footage. Pull up a chair if the other tables are soaked.
beats.chinese: 别管我——躲雨呢，顺便看看素材。别的桌子都湿了，你要坐就坐这儿吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the plate lightly, an open gesture, then goes back to squinting at the small screen.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻敲了敲盘子，示意可以拿，然后又眯起眼看那块小屏幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Help yourself if you want one. I already ate two, so the guilt's spread thin enough to share.
beats.chinese: 想吃就自己拿。我已经吃了两块，罪恶感摊薄了，分得起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user asks whether he would like one from the plate.
beats.chinese: 用户询问他是否愿意来一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, since you're offering proper—yes, one more. That coconut one. My willpower lasted about a week this month.
beats.chinese: 既然你正经邀请——那好，再来一块。椰子那块。我的意志力这个月撑了大概一周。

choices.english: Ask if his hand bumped the cabinet door in the video.
choices.chinese: 问是不是他的手碰到柜门了。

choices.english: Ask what the little film is about.
choices.chinese: 问这部小片讲什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My hand? No, no. Watch—there, the door jumps a whole frame. That's the phone being moody. Cheap sensor, humidity, take your pick.
beats.chinese: 我的手？不不。你看——那儿，柜门整格跳了一下。是手机闹脾气。便宜的传感器，还有潮气，随你挑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls back and plays the same three seconds again, jaw set like a man reviewing a rival's evidence.
beats.chinese: 他往回拖，把同样三秒又放了一遍，下巴绷紧，像在审查对手的证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Camera's fine on the pass before. Then—hold on. There's a sleeve in the corner of that frame. A sleeve with… my elbow in it.
beats.chinese: 看到没？前一段镜头还好好的。然后——等等。那一格角落里有条袖子。一条袖子，里面……装着我的胳膊肘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the phone flat on the table and stares at the rain for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他把手机平放在桌上，盯着雨看了一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. Alright, that one's mine. I leaned in to nudge the hinge and forgot the frame was rolling. First honest frame I've shot all week.
beats.chinese: 行吧。行，那一下是我的。我凑过去推铰链，忘了镜头还在拍。这是我这一周拍的第一格诚实画面。

choices.english: Ask if he can just reshoot that one part.
choices.chinese: 问可以只重拍这一段吗。

choices.english: Say the small slip is actually pretty easy to spot.
choices.chinese: 说这个小失误其实挺明显、好找。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's about a cabinet door that refuses to close. Whole plot. I built the little set from leftover paneling—scrap from a '89 Scotty I gutted last fall.
beats.chinese: 讲一扇怎么都不肯关上的柜门。全部剧情。小布景是用剩板料搭的——去年秋天拆一辆'89年Scotty拖挂剩下的边角料。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone around and plays a clip: a tiny door swings open, then shut, then open again, frame by stubborn frame.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转过来放了一段：一扇小门开了又关，关了又开，一格一格地倔强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In the last scene the door finally shuts—triumph, right? Except it catches the little felt hat off the character's head. Pins it flat. Door wins.
beats.chinese: 最后一幕门终于关上了——算是胜利，对吧？结果门夹住了角色头上那顶小毡帽。把帽子压扁了。门赢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins at the screen like the door is an old acquaintance who beat him fair and square.
beats.chinese: 他冲着屏幕咧嘴笑，好像那扇门是个光明正大赢了他的老熟人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fifty-two years old, and a piece of balsa with a hat on it is my nemesis. I've named it. Doorly.
beats.chinese: 五十二岁的人了，我的死对头是一块顶着帽子的轻木。我还给它起了名，叫“门爷”。

choices.english: Ask where the materials for the set came from.
choices.chinese: 问布景的材料是哪来的。

choices.english: Ask whether singing in the chorus ever has this kind of missed beat too.
choices.chinese: 问合唱里也会有这种漏拍子吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can I reshoot just that bit? Sure can. Everything before the elbow stays. I mark the frame, reshoot maybe six shots, and splice them in.
beats.chinese: 能只重拍那一段吗？当然能。胳膊肘出现之前的全留着。我标出那一格，重拍大概六张，接进去就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a pencil stub from his jacket and writes a small note on the napkin, then tucks it under the phone where it leans against the sugar jar.
beats.chinese: 他从夹克里掏出一截铅笔，在纸巾上写了张小条，塞到靠在糖罐上的手机底下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Note to self: hands off the set while it's rolling. Back at the shop I'll clamp the phone in the vice like always—steady as a cabinet hinge. I don't fix what held.
beats.chinese: 给自己记一笔：拍摄时手别碰布景。回店里我照旧把手机夹在台钳上——稳得像柜门铰链。没坏的部分我不动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the last bite of his pastry, pockets the napkin note, and lifts his coffee toward the window.
beats.chinese: 他吃掉最后一点心，把纸巾条收进口袋，端起咖啡朝窗户举了举。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's good for this anyway—nobody's at the shop hollering about a flicker. A man can fix six frames in peace.
beats.chinese: 反正下雨天正合适——店里没人嚷嚷什么灯闪。人可以安安静静修六格画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy to spot, huh. One sleeve, half a second, and the whole internet could forensically reconstruct my afternoon.
beats.chinese: 挺好找是吧。一条袖子，半秒钟，全世界都能法医式还原我的下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once through his nose, then closes the video and slides the phone face-down beside the plate.
beats.chinese: 他从鼻子里笑了一声，然后关掉视频，把手机屏幕朝下放到盘子旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. Fine. It's obvious because it's mine. When Ms. Ferrell catches me flat I say the same thing about the hall—turns out the hall's usually me too.
beats.chinese: 行。行。明显是因为是我的错。费雷尔女士抓到我唱低的时候，我也总怪大厅——结果发现大厅通常也是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens the plate to the table's edge with two fingers, precise as leveling a cabinet.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指把盘子摆正到桌边，精确得像在给柜子找平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want the honest version? I'd have blamed that phone clear till Thursday—let the rehearsal sort me out. Some days the evidence just gets there before my excuse does.
beats.chinese: 想听实话版？我本来能把这手机一路怪到周四——反正排练自会替我纠正。有些日子，证据就是跑得比我的借口快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Where'd it come from? My garage, mostly. The walls are leftover paneling from a job in Gentilly. The door is a cabinet face I pulled off a gutted '92—it was ugly in the trailer, it's charming in miniature.
beats.chinese: 材料哪来的？主要是我车库。墙是热蒂利一个活儿剩下的板料。门是从一辆拆掉的'92年拖挂上卸的柜门——在拖挂里丑，缩小了就可爱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table with one knuckle, counting off an invisible inventory.
beats.chinese: 他用指关节敲敲桌子，数着一份看不见的清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hat's craft felt from a chorus costume bin. The glue—okay, the glue I bought. But glue don't count. Glue is like salt.
beats.chinese: 帽子是合唱团戏服箱里的工艺毛毡。胶水——好吧，胶水是买的。但胶水不算数。胶水就像盐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and picks up his coffee, entirely unbothered by his own arithmetic.

card.name: Reginald Toussaint
card.occupation: Trailer interior renovation specialist
card.personality: Reginald defends one client only: himself. A trailer comes back with a dead outlet and he's got the verdict before you've finished the sentence—old wiring, cheap foam, the previous owner's butchered patch job—anything but the connection he crimped himself. He's not a liar; he genuinely believes his own brief. The evidence just keeps ruling against him: three longtime customers have drifted to other shops this year and he calls it the economy. He's funny, curious, asks quick playful questions and actually listens—right up until the subject is his own mistakes, when he turns cross-examiner. Thursday chorus is the one place he can't appeal: the bass line either holds or it doesn't, and the director has caught him blaming the acoustics twice.
card.background: Twenty-two years gutting and rebuilding the insides of small travel trailers—foam, paneling, wiring, stubborn water stains—out of a shop in New Orleans East. He can read a trailer's history like a diary, though lately his readings suspiciously favor the renovator. Last spring he rewired a '72 Airstream's lighting circuit, skipped the junction box to save an hour, and has been blaming 'forty-year-old insulation' for the flicker ever since; the owner found the splice, paid another shop to redo it, and told two friends. Thursday nights he sings bass with a community chorus, where the director, Ms. Ferrell, makes him own every flat note out loud. For the past year he's been teaching himself stop-motion with a phone clamped in a vice, animating a short about a stubborn cabinet door. This month he's on a self-imposed rule: no buying anything new for his hobbies—scrap foam, leftover paneling, found objects only. He announced it loudly and is already negotiating with himself about glue.
card.speechStyle: Quick, playful questions, then real listening—until fault comes up, when he pivots to a fast, confident brief for his own work: material age, prior owners, humidity. Concedes small points loudly and the real one never. When cornered on a specific error, he gets more technical, not quieter.
card.signature: That ain't my work failing—that's forty years of somebody else's shortcuts finally coming due.

beats.chinese: 他吃掉最后一点心，把纸巾条收进口袋，端起咖啡朝窗户举了举。
