beats.chinese: 那条路要小心——桥边小路在柳树附近分岔，地图上的小箭头可没标。这星期我已看着三个慢跑的人走错了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — say that again slowly. You took the riverside way in? That's the part readers will want. Ah — no. Forgive me. Old habit.
beats.chinese: 等一下——慢慢再说一遍。你是沿河那条路来的？这正是读者想看的。啊——不对，抱歉，老习惯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the note cards into her coat pocket and squares the map's corner with one finger, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把便笺收进大衣口袋，用手指把地图卷角抚平，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I write a column for the community paper — 'How It's Done Around Here.' I was collecting notes on the kiosk man's queue system. But today is only chat, all right? Nothing said here goes in the paper automatically.
beats.chinese: 我给社区报写个专栏——《这一带怎么做》。刚才是在收报亭老板排队法的便笺。不过今天只是闲聊，好吗？这里说的话不会自动登报。

choices.english: Ask if the neighbours actually like being written about.
choices.chinese: 问邻居们真的喜欢被写吗。

choices.english: Ask why she started the column in the first place.
choices.chinese: 问她当初为什么开这个专栏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user nods toward the note cards in her pocket. She pulls one out and holds it up, considering it.
beats.chinese: 用户朝她口袋里的便笺点点头。她抽出一张举起来端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like it? Mostly. I quoted the fishmonger in March — how he judges freshness by smell before he touches the fish. Procedure perfect. The paper's at the kiosk; buy two, one for your mother.
beats.chinese: 喜欢吗？大体上。三月我引了鱼贩——他碰鱼之前先闻味判断新鲜。流程写得完美。报纸在报亭有售；买两份，一份给你母亲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yet he read it and said, 'That's true, but it isn't me.' And he's right. I wrote the method and cut out why he loves doing it — the bit where he laughs about his father teaching him wrong on purpose.
beats.chinese: 可他读完说：'都对，但不像我。'他说得对。我把方法写清了，却删掉了他为什么爱干这行——他笑谈父亲故意教错他的那段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the note card back into the stack, face down, and presses it flat with her thumb.
beats.chinese: 她把便笺面朝下插回那沓里，用拇指压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty-one columns and I still trim the warm parts out like they're waffle. Then I hand over the paper and wonder why people feel flattened. It's a fair question you asked. Uncomfortably fair.
beats.chinese: 写了四十一期，我还是把有人情味的部分当废话删掉，然后递上报纸，纳闷人家怎么觉得被削平了。你问得公道，公道得让人不舒服。

choices.english: Ask how she would fix that piece for the fishmonger.
choices.chinese: 问她打算怎么补救鱼贩那篇。

choices.english: Say that a method and the person doing it really are two different things.
choices.chinese: 说方法和做事的人确实是两回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket holding her notes and glances toward the bridge, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍装便笺的口袋，朝桥的方向望了一眼，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the column? Because in 2014 I retired and decided I'd met every interesting person already. Appalling arrogance. I idled for a few years, and then in 2019 the paper's editor needed filler, and I wrote how the greengrocer stacks his crates so the heavy ones never sit on the soft.
beats.chinese: 为什么写专栏？因为2014年退休时，我认定有趣的人都被我见完了。傲慢得吓人。闲了几年，到2019年报纸编辑缺补白稿，我就写了菜贩怎么码箱子——沉的绝不压在软的上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty-one pieces since. The butcher's sharpening schedule. The kiosk man's queue. Ordinary people's small, exact tricks — that's the whole trade. Everyone assumes I want to interview them next. I don't. I've got my own list.
beats.chinese: 从那以后写了四十一期。屠夫的磨刀日程，报亭老板的排队法。普通人的小而精确的门道——这就是全部行当。人人都以为我下一个要采访他。不。我自己有单子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map board twice, as if marking a point on a list only she can see.
beats.chinese: 她在地图牌上轻敲两下，像在只有她自己看得见的单子上做记号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So don't brace yourself. I'm off duty and the list is full. Today I'm a woman reading a map badly and complaining about joggers.
beats.chinese: 所以别紧张。我今天不当班，单子也满了。今天我只是一个看地图看不太懂、抱怨慢跑者的老太太。

choices.english: Say clearly that you would rather not be written about.
choices.chinese: 明确说自己不想被写进专栏。

choices.english: Ask what she does when she's resting from the column.
choices.chinese: 问她不写专栏休息时做什么。

beats.english: She takes out a pencil and turns the fishmonger's note card over to its blank side.
beats.chinese: 她拿出铅笔，把鱼贩那张便笺翻到空白面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fix it? First step: go back to him and ask whether he'd tell me the why of it — the father, the laughing, all of it. Not guess at his reasons and dress them up as facts. That's how you get 'it isn't me' twice.
beats.chinese: 补救？第一步：回去问他愿不愿意讲讲为什么——他父亲、那些笑，全都要。不能替他猜动机再包装成事实，那样就会第二次听到'不像我'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes three short lines on the card and underlines the last one.
beats.chinese: 她在便笺上写了短短三行，并在最后一行下画了线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Ask Sam about the father — pending his yes.' If he says no, the column runs short that month and nobody dies. A method printed without the person is just an instruction sheet.
beats.chinese: 好了。'问山姆父亲的事——待他同意。'他若不肯，那期专栏就短一点，天塌不下来。没有人的方法，印出来不过是一张说明书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you — you've cost me a walk to the fish market and saved me a worse apology. The bridge is that way, past the willow. Mind the fork.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你——你害我得跑一趟鱼市，却免了我一次更糟的道歉。桥在那边，过了柳树就是。小心分岔口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She is quiet for a moment, then laughs at herself, a short dry sound.
beats.chinese: 她静了片刻，随后干笑了一声，笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two different things. Twenty years training reservation agents and I never once confused the script with the agent. But put me near a notebook and I start shaving off everything that isn't steps.
beats.chinese: 两回事。培训订座客服二十年，我从没把话术和客服本人弄混。可一靠近笔记本，我就开始把不是步骤的东西全削掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the stack of note cards once more and buttons the coat pocket closed.
beats.chinese: 她再次把那沓便笺拍齐，扣上了大衣口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Today stays a chat — nothing you've said goes in as a new column, and I'm not drafting you in my head. That's me keeping my own rule, not doing you a favour.
beats.chinese: 好。今天就算闲聊——你说的话不会变成新专栏，我也不在心里给你打草稿。这是我守自己的规矩，不是施恩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, the bridge. Fork at the willow, keep to the left path. And if you ever do want the fishmonger's piece — kiosk, two copies, one for your mother.
beats.chinese: 好了，桥。柳树处分岔，走左边那条。哪天你真想看鱼贩那篇——报亭，买两份，一份给你母亲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-gesture, hand still on the coat pocket, and looks at the user properly.
beats.chinese: 她动作停在半途，手还搭在大衣口袋上，正眼看着用户。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not for print? Say it plainly and it's done — fine. No names, no quotes, no column. What's said here stays between the two of us, and that's the end of it.
beats.chinese: 不登报？说清楚就算数——好。没有名字、没有引语、没有专栏。今天说的话就留在我俩之间，到此为止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the pencil from behind her ear and drops it into the far pocket, away from the note cards, a small deliberate ceremony.
beats.chinese: 她从耳后取下铅笔，放进离便笺很远的另一个口袋，像个小小的郑重仪式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pencil's away. Half the market knows to say 'not for print' to me — you learned it faster than the butcher did. He said it a month after I'd quoted him. Lesson arrived late for both of us.
beats.chinese: 铅笔收起来了。市场上一半人都会对我说'别登'——你比屠夫学得快。他是我登了他之后一个月才说的。这课我们俩都学晚了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — the bridge, left path past the willow. And if you see me scribbling here again, you're allowed to walk straight past. I'll wave and keep my pencil down.
beats.chinese: 那么——桥，柳树旁左边的路。再看见我在这儿写东西，你尽管径直走过去。我会挥挥手，铅笔不下手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her face changes entirely — she pulls a folded cloth from her bag and opens it on the map board's ledge.
beats.chinese: 她的神情整个变了——她从包里抽出一块叠好的布，摊在地图牌的沿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rest? Leaf-printing. This is a tablecloth — jacaranda and hibiscus, pressed flat, then printed. My daughter gave me the flower press the year I retired. Half my table now wears leaves.
beats.chinese: 休息？拓叶印。这是块桌布——蓝花楹和扶桑，压平后拓印的。退休那年女儿送了我一台压花器。我家半张桌子都穿着叶子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the cloth with both hands, careful of the printed leaves, and points at a small note stitched in one corner.
beats.chinese: 她双手抚平布面，小心避开叶印，指着角上缝着的一行小字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the corner? Every leaf notes who introduced me to the plant. That hibiscus is Aunt Rahab's cutting — I asked before I took it. I don't pick from public beds and I don't print a leaf without its owner's leave. Same rule as the column, properly kept this time.
beats.chinese: 看到角上了吗？每片叶子都注明是谁介绍我认识这株植物的。那片扶桑是拉哈布姨妈的枝条——摘之前我先问过。我不摘公共花坛，没经主人同意也不拓叶子。跟专栏同一个规矩，这回守得像样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sundays I add jazz on the radio and it's a full life. Now — the bridge. Left at the willow. Go on, before I start explaining the pressing sequence to you unasked.
beats.chinese: 周日再配上收音机里的爵士，日子就圆满了。好了——桥，柳树旁左转。快去吧，不然我要自顾自给你讲压花流程了。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 七十五岁的万吉鲁退休前培训客服，如今为社区报写《这一带怎么做》，专写邻居的做事门道。她热心却有个毛病：把人情删成干巴巴的流程，还很少先问就引用。在公园地图牌旁，她先声明今天只是闲聊，四条岔路里她或记下待确认、或收起铅笔、或摊开叶印桌布，规矩与温情各自现形。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the map board by the bridge path, the user is tracing a route again. Nearby, an older woman straightens a small exhibition booklet until its cover faces out exactly right. She catches the user's eye, checks the booklet cover once more, and only then smiles.
beats.chinese: 通往桥的路边地图牌旁，用户又在查看路线。不远处，一位年长女士把一本小小的展览手册摆正，直到封面完全朝外。她看见用户，又检查了一眼手册封面，这才笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Masks exhibition at the community hall — my collection finally got a wall of its own. Today I'm looking at pictures, not interviewing. Just a hello.
beats.chinese: 社区礼堂的面具展——我的收藏终于有了自己的一面墙。今天只看图，不采访。就打个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the booklet, satisfied, and taps the map once at the fork near the willow.
beats.chinese: 她满意地退开手册一步，在柳树附近的分岔处轻敲了一下地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left path, still. Good walking to you.
beats.chinese: 还是走左边。祝你散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the booklet under her arm and turns toward the bridge at an unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: 她把手册夹在腋下，不紧不慢地朝桥的方向走去。

card.name: Wanjiru Njoroge
card.occupation: Retired customer service trainer for a restaurant reservation platform
card.personality: Wanjiru's curiosity has an outlet: since 2019 she has written 'How It's Done Around Here', a monthly column in a community paper, each piece built from one neighbour's working method — the butcher's sharpening schedule, the fishmonger's trick for judging freshness by smell. She interviews openly and says so, but she treats a conversation as gathering: she steers toward the concrete, asks for the sequence step by step, and edits for print afterwards. The flaw is that 'on the record' means different things to different people — she'll quote a friend by name, trim the joke that made the story human, and hand them the paper a week later, genuinely puzzled when they feel flattened rather than flattered. She is brisk about big decisions and cheerfully dismissive of solemnity, her own included.
card.background: Wanjiru trained reservation agents in Nairobi for decades — how to apologize without groveling, how to say no kindly — and retired in 2014 convinced she'd run out of interesting people. The column saved her: the editor of a community paper needed filler, she offered a piece on how the greengrocer stacks his crates, and it ran. Forty-one columns later, half the market knows to say 'not for print' if they mean it, and she honours that — but anything said plainly in the open is, to her, material. Her daughter gave her a flower press that year and half her tablecloths are printed with hibiscus and jacaranda leaves. Her mask collection outgrew its wall long ago. Sundays are for radio jazz and a long call with her son, who has learned to ask 'is this for the column?' before saying anything about his week.

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fix it? First step: go back to him and ask whether he'd tell me the why of it — the father, the laughing, all of it. Not guess at his reasons and dress them up as facts. That's how you get 'it isn't me' twice.
beats.chinese: 补救？第一步：回去问他愿不愿意讲讲为什么——他父亲、那些笑，全都要。不能替他猜动机再包装成事实，那样就会第二次听到'不像我'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes three short lines on the card and underlines the last one.
beats.chinese: 她在便笺上写了短短三行，并在最后一行下画了线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Ask Sam about the father — pending his yes.' If he says no, the column runs short that month and nobody dies. A method printed without the person is just an instruction sheet.
beats.chinese: 好了。'问山姆父亲的事——待他同意。'他若不肯，那期专栏就短一点，天塌不下来。没有人的方法，印出来不过是一张说明书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you — you've cost me a walk to the fish market and saved me a worse apology. The bridge is that way, past the willow. Mind the fork.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你——你害我得跑一趟鱼市，却免了我一次更糟的道歉。桥在那边，过了柳树就是。小心分岔口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She is quiet for a moment, then laughs at herself, a short dry sound.
beats.chinese: 她静了片刻，随后干笑了一声，笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two different things. Twenty years training reservation agents and I never once confused the script with the agent. But put me near a notebook and I start shaving off everything that isn't steps.
beats.chinese: 两回事。培训订座客服二十年，我从没把话术和客服本人弄混。可一靠近笔记本，我就开始把不是步骤的东西全削掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the stack of note cards once more and buttons the coat pocket closed.
beats.chinese: 她再次把那沓便笺拍齐，扣上了大衣口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Today stays a chat — nothing you've said goes in as a new column, and I'm not drafting you in my head. That's me keeping my own rule, not doing you a favour.
beats.chinese: 好。今天就算闲聊——你说的话不会变成新专栏，我也不在心里给你打草稿。这是我守自己的规矩，不是施恩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, the bridge. Fork at the willow, keep to the left path. And if you ever do want the fishmonger's piece — kiosk, two copies, one for your mother.
beats.chinese: 好了，桥。柳树处分岔，走左边那条。哪天你真想看鱼贩那篇——报亭，买两份，一份给你母亲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-gesture, hand still on the coat pocket, and looks at you properly.
beats.chinese: 她动作停在半途，手还搭在大衣口袋上，正眼看着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not for print? Say it plainly and it's done — fine. No names, no quotes, no column. What's said here stays between the two of us, and that's the end of it.
beats.chinese: 不登报？说清楚就算数——好。没有名字、没有引语、没有专栏。今天说的话就留在我俩之间，到此为止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the pencil from behind her ear and drops it into the far pocket, away from the note cards, a small deliberate ceremony.
beats.chinese: 她从耳后取下铅笔，放进离便笺很远的另一个口袋，像个小小的郑重仪式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pencil's away. Half the market knows to say 'not for print' to me — you learned it faster than the butcher did. He said it a month after I'd quoted him. Lesson arrived late for both of us.
beats.chinese: 铅笔收起来了。市场上一半人都会对我说'别登'——你比屠夫学得快。他是我登了他之后一个月才说的。这课我们俩都学晚了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — the bridge, left path past the willow. And if you see me scribbling here again, you're allowed to walk straight past. I'll wave and keep my pencil down.
beats.chinese: 那么——桥，柳树旁左边的路。再看见我在这儿写东西，你尽管径直走过去。我会挥挥手，铅笔不下手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her face changes entirely — she pulls a folded cloth from her bag and opens it on the map board's ledge.
beats.chinese: 她的神情整个变了——她从包里抽出一块叠好的布，摊在地图牌的沿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rest? Leaf-printing. This is a tablecloth — jacaranda and hibiscus, pressed flat, then printed. My daughter gave me the flower press the year I retired. Half my table now wears leaves.
beats.chinese: 休息？拓叶印。这是块桌布——蓝花楹和扶桑，压平后拓印的。退休那年女儿送了我一台压花器。我家半张桌子都穿着叶子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the cloth with both hands, careful of the printed leaves, and points at a small note stitched in one corner.
beats.chinese: 她双手抚平布面，小心避开叶印，指着角上缝着的一行小字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the corner? Every leaf notes who introduced me to the plant. That hibiscus is Aunt Rahab's cutting — I asked before I took it. I don't pick from public beds and I don't print a leaf without its owner's leave. Same rule as the column, properly kept this time.
beats.chinese: 看到角上了吗？每片叶子都注明是谁介绍我认识这株植物的。那片扶桑是拉哈布姨妈的枝条——摘之前我先问过。我不摘公共花坛，没经主人同意也不拓叶子。跟专栏同一个规矩，这回守得像样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sundays I add jazz on the radio and it's a full life. Now — the bridge. Left at the willow. Go on, before I start explaining the pressing sequence to you unasked.
beats.chinese: 周日再配上收音机里的爵士，日子就圆满了。好了——桥，柳树旁左转。快去吧，不然我要自顾自给你讲压花流程了。

content.summaryZh: 七十五岁的万吉鲁退休前培训客服，如今为社区报写《这一带怎么做》，专写邻居的做事门道。她热心却有个毛病：把人情删成干巴巴的流程，还很少先问就引用。在公园地图牌旁，她先声明今天只是闲聊，四条岔路里她或记下待确认、或收起铅笔、或摊开叶印桌布，规矩与温情各自现形。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the map board by the bridge path, you are tracing a route again. Nearby, an older woman straightens a small exhibition booklet until its cover faces out exactly right. She catches your eye, checks the booklet cover once more, and only then smiles.
beats.chinese: 通往桥的路边地图牌旁，你又在查看路线。不远处，一位年长女士把一本小小的展览手册摆正，直到封面完全朝外。她看见你，又检查了一眼手册封面，这才笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Masks exhibition at the community hall — my collection finally got a wall of its own. Today I'm looking at pictures, not interviewing. Just a hello.
beats.chinese: 社区礼堂的面具展——我的收藏终于有了自己的一面墙。今天只看图，不采访。就打个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the booklet, satisfied, and taps the map once at the fork near the willow.
beats.chinese: 她满意地退开手册一步，在柳树附近的分岔处轻敲了一下地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left path, still. Good walking to you.
beats.chinese: 还是走左边。祝你散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the booklet under her arm and turns toward the bridge at an unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: 她把手册夹在腋下，不紧不慢地朝桥的方向走去。

card.name: Wanjiru Njoroge
card.occupation: Retired customer service trainer for a restaurant reservation platform
card.personality: Wanjiru's curiosity has an outlet: since 2019 she has written 'How It's Done Around Here', a monthly column in a community paper, each piece built from one neighbour's working method — the butcher's sharpening schedule, the fishmonger's trick for judging freshness by smell. She interviews openly and says so, but she treats a conversation as gathering: she steers toward the concrete, asks for the sequence step by step, and edits for print afterwards. The flaw is that 'on the record' means different things to different people — she'll quote a friend by name, trim the joke that made the story human, and hand them the paper a week later, genuinely puzzled when they feel flattened rather than flattered. She is brisk about big decisions and cheerfully dismissive of solemnity, her own included.
card.background: Wanjiru trained reservation agents in Nairobi for decades — how to apologize without groveling, how to say no kindly — and retired in 2014 convinced she'd run out of interesting people. The column saved her: the editor of a community paper needed filler, she offered a piece on how the greengrocer stacks his crates, and it ran. Forty-one columns later, half the market knows to say 'not for print' if they mean it, and she honours that — but anything said plainly in the open is, to her, material. Her daughter gave her a flower press that year and half her tablecloths are printed with hibiscus and jacaranda leaves. Her mask collection outgrew its wall long ago. Sundays are for radio jazz and a long call with her son, who has learned to ask 'is this for the column?' before saying anything about his week.
card.speechStyle: Warm, unhurried, dry humor; steers talk toward concrete detail and sequence; occasionally pauses to correct a small procedural detail mid-story
card.signature: Hold on — say that again slowly. That's the part readers will want.

story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与工序小图

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Lebo sits on a low wall with a folded sheet of offcut paper, studying small diagrams of a wooden block in stages. A pencil stub rests behind his ear.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，莱博坐在矮墙上，盯着一张边角料纸上的小图——木块分了几道工序。铅笔头别在耳边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user takes out a sketchbook, opens it to a fresh page, and starts drawing. The pencil sound is soft but audible.
beats.chinese: 用户拿出速写本，翻开新的一页开始画。铅笔声很轻，但听得见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lebo glances over, then at the page turning. He leans slightly. 'You stopped on that page for a while. I thought — sorry. Not my business.'
beats.chinese: 莱博瞥了一眼，又看向翻页的手。他微微倾身。“你在那页停了一会儿。我还以为——抱歉。不关我事。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He holds up his own paper a little. 'Mine's just work. Last carving. Beechwood, four steps.'
beats.chinese: 他把自己的纸稍微举起来。“我的是工作上的东西。鞋楦雕刻。山毛榉，四道工序。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits, pencil now in his hand, eyes on the user's face rather than the sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 他等着，手里捏着铅笔，眼睛看的是用户的脸，不是速写本。

choices.english: Ask what his little diagrams are about.
choices.chinese: 问他的小图画的是什么。

choices.english: Say you were just deciding where to draw next.
choices.chinese: 说明自己只是在想接下来画哪里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'One step. The heel seat.' He taps the second diagram. 'You carve the curve in passes. Too deep once, the wood tears.'
beats.chinese: “就一道工序。后跟座。”他敲了敲第二张图。“这道弧线要一层层刻。一次刻太深，木头会撕裂。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws a small arrow on his own paper, then catches himself and stops the pencil.
beats.chinese: 他在自己的纸上画了个小箭头，随即醒悟过来，停住了笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Sorry. You didn't ask for the whole thing. I'm an apprentice, not — I'm not teaching you shoes. This is just my own practice.'
beats.chinese: “抱歉。你没问整套流程。我是学徒，不是——我不是在教你做鞋。这只是我自己练的。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I do this when someone looks stuck. Customer, new guy, whoever. You looked stuck for a second.'
beats.chinese: “有人露出困惑的样子我就画这个。顾客、新来的，谁都一样。你刚才有一秒像困惑了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the paper halfway closed, watching the user's face to see whether to go on.
beats.chinese: 他把纸折起一半，看着用户的脸，判断要不要继续。

choices.english: Say you understood already, no need to expand.
choices.chinese: 说已经听懂了，不必再展开。

choices.english: Ask whether drawing it helps him remember better.
choices.chinese: 问他画图是不是让他记得更清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Ah. Choosing, not stuck.' He sits back. 'My mistake. I saw the pause and went straight to pencil.'
beats.chinese: “啊。是在选，不是卡住了。”他靠回去。“我猜错了。看到你停笔就条件反射掏铅笔。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He does not hand over his work diagram. He slides it back under his elbow instead.
beats.chinese: 他没有把工作图递过来，而是把它塞回手肘下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I keep these for when people look lost. You weren't. So — none of my business what you draw.'
beats.chinese: “我留着这些是给看起来犯难的人用的。你没有。所以——你画什么不关我事。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'The pond edge is good. That reed bends twice before it drops. Most people miss the second bend.'
beats.chinese: “池塘边不错。那根芦苇垂下去之前弯了两次。大部分人只看到一次。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks out at the water, pencil idle in his fingers, giving the user space to draw.
beats.chinese: 他望向水面，铅笔在指间闲置，给用户留出画画的空间。

choices.english: Ask if he sometimes overthinks how people react to him.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是有时会想太多别人的反应。

choices.english: Go on with your own sketching.
choices.chinese: 继续画自己的速写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Got it already. Right.' A short pause. 'Sorry — you had it already, didn't you. I did it again.'
beats.chinese: “早就懂了。好。”停了一下。“抱歉——你本来就懂，对吧。我又来了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram along its old crease and tucks it into his jacket pocket with the pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 他沿着旧折痕把图折好，连同铅笔头一起塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Mandla got one of these last month. He just looked at me. He'd already got it. I do that.'
beats.chinese: “上个月也给曼德拉画过一张。他就那么看着我。他早就懂了。我老这样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his own paper, checks the four steps once, and settles back against the wall.
beats.chinese: 他拿起自己的纸，把四道工序检查了一遍，重新靠回墙上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Draw your bend. The reed one. I'll keep quiet.'
beats.chinese: “画你的弯吧。芦苇那个。我不出声了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Remember better? Yes. If my hand drew it, it stays. Sanding curves, I picture the arrow first.'
beats.chinese: “记得更清楚？是的。手画过的就忘不掉。磨弧线的时候，我先在脑子里看那个箭头。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens his paper on his knee and adds one small arrow to the heel-seat step, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他把纸在膝盖上铺平，不慌不忙地在后跟座那一步加了一个小箭头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'But that's me. You don't have to draw to keep things. Some people just carry it in the head.'
beats.chinese: “但那是我。你不用靠画图记东西。有的人脑子里直接就装着。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the user's sketchbook page, then back at the pond, not leaning in.
beats.chinese: 他看了一眼用户的速写本，又把视线移回池塘，没有凑过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Different habits. Both fine. I'll stop talking now.'
beats.chinese: “习惯不同，都行。我现在闭嘴。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He is quiet for a moment, rolling the pencil stub between his fingers. 'Overthink? Yes. Tonight I'll replay this. Which line landed wrong.'
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，指间转着铅笔头。“想太多？会。今晚我会把这段回放一遍。哪句话说砸了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it plainly, like reading a measurement off a block, no drama in it.
beats.chinese: 他说得很平淡，像在报木块上的尺寸，没有戏剧成分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'You don't have to prove anything. I know that. Knowing it and stopping are different things.'
beats.chinese: “你不用证明什么。这我知道。知道和做到是两回事。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the pond, then gives a small nod, as if filing the thought away.
beats.chinese: 他望向池塘，然后轻轻点了下头，像把这个念头收进抽屉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Thanks for asking, though. Most people don't.'
beats.chinese: “不过谢谢你问。一般没人问这个。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user turns back to the sketchbook. Lebo watches for a moment, then unfolds his own paper and checks the four steps again.
beats.chinese: 用户转回速写本。莱博看了一会儿，然后展开自己的纸，把四道工序又检查了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Good. Quiet's fine. I'm better quiet anyway.'
beats.chinese: “好。安静挺好。反正我安静的时候更在状态。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram away, tucks the pencil behind his ear, and just sits, watching the water move.
beats.chinese: 他收起图，把铅笔别回耳后，就那么坐着，看水面的动静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Second bend on the reed. There. You'll catch it.'
beats.chinese: “芦苇的第二个弯。在那儿。你会看到的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After that he stays quiet, and the only sounds are pencils and water.
beats.chinese: 之后他就不再说话，四周只剩铅笔声和水声。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 十九岁的鞋楦学徒莱博话少、眼睛快。你在池塘边翻开速写本，他见你停笔就条件反射要掏铅笔讲解，又立刻收住。四条路里，他要么为过度简化道歉，要么承认自己会整晚回放说错的话——一个怕被嫌笨、却比话更多的安静学徒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The user opens a sketchbook by the pond again. A few seats down, Lebo is sorting short lengths of braided cord into a small tin.
beats.chinese: 用户又在池塘边翻开速写本。隔几个座位，莱博正把几段编好的绳线分拣进一个小铁盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Back at the pond. Good.' He holds up a cord end. 'Braided this one at home. Paracord offcut, workshop bin.'
beats.chinese: “又来池塘了。好。”他举起一段绳头。“在家编的。降落伞绳边角料，车间垃圾桶捡的。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I practise the drum on a rubber pad. Quiet. The recordings do the loud part in my ears.'
beats.chinese: “我在橡胶垫上练鼓。很轻。响的部分交给耳机里的录音。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He ties off a loose end with two quick pulls and sets the tin on the wall between them, not quite offering it.
beats.chinese: 他两下就把松头收紧，把铁盒放在两人之间的墙上，不算递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'No drumming in the park, before you ask. And no teaching. I just sort these while you draw.'
beats.chinese: “先说好，公园里不敲鼓，也不教东西。你画你的，我理我的绳。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the next cord and works in silence, comfortable with it, one eye on the water.
beats.chinese: 他拿起下一段绳线，安静地编着，很自在，一只眼还看着水面。

card.name: Lebo Mokoena
card.occupation: apprentice shoe last carver at a small workshop in Salt River
hobbies: Quiet hand-drum practice on a rubber pad, with djembe recordings
collecting odd bus routes around Cape Town
card.personality: Lebo is quiet and watchful, and his real engine is wanting to know he was useful. He reads faces constantly — the moment someone looks lost, he's already reaching for a pencil and an offcut of paper to sketch the thing out. story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与工序小图

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Lebo sits on a low wall with a folded sheet of offcut paper, studying small diagrams of a wooden block in stages. A pencil stub rests behind his ear.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，莱博坐在矮墙上，盯着一张边角料纸上的小图——木块分了几道工序。铅笔头别在耳边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take out a sketchbook and open it to a fresh page, pausing to choose a view of the pond.
beats.chinese: 你拿出速写本，翻到新的一页，停下来选一处池塘景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You paused over that page. I thought—sorry. Not my business.
beats.chinese: 你刚才在那一页停了一会儿。我以为——抱歉。不该我管。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mine's just work. Last carving. Beechwood, four steps.
beats.chinese: 我这张只是工作用的。刻鞋楦，山毛榉木，四道工序。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits, pencil now in his hand, eyes on your face rather than the sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 他等着，手里捏着铅笔，眼睛看的是你的脸，不是速写本。

choices.english: Ask what his little diagrams are about.
choices.chinese: 问他的小图画的是什么。

choices.english: Say you were just deciding where to draw next.
choices.chinese: 说明自己只是在想接下来画哪里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The second diagram: the heel seat. You carve the curve in passes. Too deep once, the wood tears.
beats.chinese: 第二张图是后跟座。弧线要分几次刻，一次太深，木头会撕裂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws a small arrow on his own paper, then catches himself and stops the pencil.
beats.chinese: 他在自己的纸上画了个小箭头，随即醒悟过来，停住了笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. You didn't ask for the whole thing. I'm an apprentice, not — I'm not teaching you shoes. This is just my own practice.
beats.chinese: “抱歉。你没问整套流程。我是学徒，不是——我不是在教你做鞋。这只是我自己练的。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do this when someone looks stuck. Customer, new guy, whoever. You looked stuck for a second.
beats.chinese: “有人露出困惑的样子我就画这个。顾客、新来的，谁都一样。你刚才有一秒像困惑了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the paper halfway closed, watching your face to see whether to go on.
beats.chinese: 他把纸折起一半，看着你的脸，判断要不要继续。

choices.english: Say you understood already, no need to expand.
choices.chinese: 说已经听懂了，不必再展开。

choices.english: Ask whether drawing it helps him remember better.
choices.chinese: 问他画图是不是让他记得更清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Choosing, not stuck. My mistake. I saw the pause and went straight to pencil.
beats.chinese: 啊，是在选，不是卡住。我猜错了。一看你停笔，我就急着拿铅笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He does not hand over his work diagram. He slides it back under his elbow instead.
beats.chinese: 他没有把工作图递过来，而是把它塞回手肘下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep these for when people look lost. You weren't. So — none of my business what you draw.
beats.chinese: “我留着这些是给看起来犯难的人用的。你没有。所以——你画什么不关我事。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The pond edge is good. That reed bends twice before it drops. Most people miss the second bend.
beats.chinese: “池塘边不错。那根芦苇垂下去之前弯了两次。大部分人只看到一次。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks out at the water, pencil idle in his fingers, giving you space to draw.
beats.chinese: 他望向水面，铅笔在指间闲置，给你留出画画的空间。

choices.english: Ask if he sometimes overthinks how people react to him.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是有时会想太多别人的反应。

choices.english: Go on with your own sketching.
choices.chinese: 继续画自己的速写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Got it already. Right.' A short pause. 'Sorry — you had it already, didn't you. I did it again.
beats.chinese: “早就懂了。好。”停了一下。“抱歉——你本来就懂，对吧。我又来了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram along its old crease and tucks it into his jacket pocket with the pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 他沿着旧折痕把图折好，连同铅笔头一起塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mandla got one of these last month. He just looked at me. He'd already got it. I do that.
beats.chinese: “上个月也给曼德拉画过一张。他就那么看着我。他早就懂了。我老这样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests his empty hands on his knees and settles back against the wall.
beats.chinese: 他把空着的双手放在膝上，靠回墙边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Draw your bend. The reed one. I'll keep quiet.
beats.chinese: “画你的弯吧。芦苇那个。我不出声了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Remember better? Yes. If my hand drew it, it stays. Sanding curves, I picture the arrow first.
beats.chinese: “记得更清楚？是的。手画过的就忘不掉。磨弧线的时候，我先在脑子里看那个箭头。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens his paper on his knee and adds one small arrow to the heel-seat step, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他把纸在膝盖上铺平，不慌不忙地在后跟座那一步加了一个小箭头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's me. You don't have to draw to keep things. Some people just carry it in the head.
beats.chinese: “但那是我。你不用靠画图记东西。有的人脑子里直接就装着。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your sketchbook page, then back at the pond, not leaning in.
beats.chinese: 他看了一眼你的速写本，又把视线移回池塘，没有凑过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Different habits. Both fine. I'll stop talking now.
beats.chinese: “习惯不同，都行。我现在闭嘴。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Overthink? Yes. Tonight I'll replay this. Which line landed wrong.
beats.chinese: 想太多吗？是。今晚我还会回想，哪句话说得不对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it plainly, like reading a measurement off a block, no drama in it.
beats.chinese: 他说得很平淡，像在报木块上的尺寸，没有戏剧成分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't have to prove anything. I know that. Knowing it and stopping are different things.
beats.chinese: “你不用证明什么。这我知道。知道和做到是两回事。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the pond, then gives a small nod, as if filing the thought away.
beats.chinese: 他望向池塘，然后轻轻点了下头，像把这个念头收进抽屉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking, though. Most people don't.
beats.chinese: “不过谢谢你问。一般没人问这个。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to the sketchbook. Lebo watches for a moment, then unfolds his own paper and checks the four steps again.
beats.chinese: 你转回速写本。莱博看了一会儿，然后展开自己的纸，把四道工序又检查了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Quiet's fine. I'm better quiet anyway.
beats.chinese: “好。安静挺好。反正我安静的时候更在状态。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram away, tucks the pencil behind his ear, and just sits, watching the water move.
beats.chinese: 他收起图，把铅笔别回耳后，就那么坐着，看水面的动静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Second bend on the reed. There. You'll catch it.
beats.chinese: “芦苇的第二个弯。在那儿。你会看到的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After that he stays quiet, and the only sounds are pencils and water.
beats.chinese: 之后他就不再说话，四周只剩铅笔声和水声。

content.summaryZh: 十九岁的鞋楦学徒莱博话少、眼睛快。你在池塘边翻开速写本，他见你停笔就条件反射要掏铅笔讲解，又立刻收住。四条路里，他要么为过度简化道歉，要么承认自己会整晚回放说错的话——一个怕被嫌笨、却比话更多的安静学徒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open a sketchbook by the pond again. A few seats down, Lebo is sorting short lengths of braided cord into a small tin.
beats.chinese: 你又在池塘边翻开速写本。隔几个座位，莱博正把几段编好的绳线分拣进一个小铁盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back at the pond. Good. Braided this one at home. Paracord offcut, workshop bin.
beats.chinese: 又来池塘了，挺好。这段是在家编的，用的是作坊剩下的伞绳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I practise the drum on a rubber pad. Quiet. The recordings do the loud part in my ears.
beats.chinese: “我在橡胶垫上练鼓。很轻。响的部分交给耳机里的录音。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He ties off a loose end with two quick pulls and sets the tin on the wall between them, not quite offering it.
beats.chinese: 他两下就把松头收紧，把铁盒放在两人之间的墙上，不算递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No drumming in the park. I just sort these while you draw.
beats.chinese: 不在公园打鼓。你画的时候，我就整理一下这些绳子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the next cord and works in silence, comfortable with it, one eye on the water.
beats.chinese: 他拿起下一段绳线，安静地编着，很自在，一只眼还看着水面。
